[134](https://docs.rs#134)/// The `FileId → FileText` side table. `Arc`-backed so a cheap clone shares the same map —
[135](https://docs.rs#135)/// needed to mutate an input (`&mut dyn Db`) without simultaneously borrowing `self.files`.
[136](https://docs.rs#136)#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
[137](https://docs.rs#137)pub struct Files {
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    inner: Arc<DashMap<FileId, FileText, FxBuildHasher>>,
[139](https://docs.rs#139)}
[140](https://docs.rs#140)
[141](https://docs.rs#141)impl Files {
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    /// The input for `file`, if set.
[143](https://docs.rs#143)    #[must_use]
[144](https://docs.rs#144)    pub fn file_text(&self, file: FileId) -> Option<FileText> {
[145](https://docs.rs#145)        self.inner.get(&file).map(|r| *r)
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    }
[147](https://docs.rs#147)
[148](https://docs.rs#148)    /// Create or update `file`'s text input at `durability`. Creating uses `&db`; updating an
[149](https://docs.rs#149)    /// existing input bumps the revision (`&mut db`), which is what cancels live read handles.
[150](https://docs.rs#150)    pub fn set_file_text(&self, db: &mut dyn Db, file: FileId, text: &str, durability: Durability) {
[151](https://docs.rs#151)        match self.inner.entry(file) {
[152](https://docs.rs#152)            Entry::Occupied(occ) => {
[153](https://docs.rs#153)                occ.get()
[154](https://docs.rs#154)                    .set_text(db)
[155](https://docs.rs#155)                    .with_durability(durability)
[156](https://docs.rs#156)                    .to(Arc::from(text));
[157](https://docs.rs#157)            }
[158](https://docs.rs#158)            Entry::Vacant(vac) => {
[159](https://docs.rs#159)                let ft = FileText::builder(Arc::from(text), file, None)
[160](https://docs.rs#160)                    .durability(durability)
[161](https://docs.rs#161)                    .new(db);
[162](https://docs.rs#162)                vac.insert(ft);
[163](https://docs.rs#163)            }
[164](https://docs.rs#164)        }
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    }
[166](https://docs.rs#166)
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    /// Set `file`'s `res://` path at `MEDIUM` durability (stable project structure, like the
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    /// source root). No-op if the file is unknown or the path is unchanged: salsa does **not**
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    /// value-backdate an input setter (it bumps the field revision on *every* call, even for an
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    /// identical value — verified against salsa 0.27.1 `input.rs:set_field`), so a redundant set
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    /// would needlessly invalidate the `res_path_registry`. The guard keeps a re-`apply_change`
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    /// of an already-known path free.
[173](https://docs.rs#173)    pub fn set_file_path(&self, db: &mut dyn Db, file: FileId, path: &str) {
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        let Some(ft) = self.inner.get(&file).map(|r| *r) else {
[175](https://docs.rs#175)            return;
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        };
[177](https://docs.rs#177)        if ft.res_path(&*db).as_deref() == Some(path) {
[178](https://docs.rs#178)            return;
[179](https://docs.rs#179)        }
[180](https://docs.rs#180)        ft.set_res_path(db)
[181](https://docs.rs#181)            .with_durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[182](https://docs.rs#182)            .to(Some(smol_str::SmolStr::new(path)));
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    }
[184](https://docs.rs#184)
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    /// Drop `file` from the side table (its salsa input lingers, unreferenced, until GC).
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    pub fn remove(&self, file: FileId) {
[187](https://docs.rs#187)        self.inner.remove(&file);
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    }
[189](https://docs.rs#189)
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    /// Every file, ordered by `FileId` — the deterministic input to project-wide queries.
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    fn all(&self) -> Vec<FileText> {
[192](https://docs.rs#192)        let mut v: Vec<(FileId, FileText)> =
[193](https://docs.rs#193)            self.inner.iter().map(|r| (*r.key(), *r.value())).collect();
[194](https://docs.rs#194)        v.sort_by_key(|(id, _)| *id);
[195](https://docs.rs#195)        v.into_iter().map(|(_, ft)| ft).collect()
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    }
[197](https://docs.rs#197)}
[198](https://docs.rs#198)

[200](https://docs.rs#200)#[salsa::tracked]
[201](https://docs.rs#201)pub fn parse(db: &dyn Db, file: FileText) -> Parse {
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    gdscript_syntax::parse(file.text(db))

[205](https://docs.rs#205)/// The concrete analyzer database — a salsa `Storage` plus the [`Files`] side table.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)#[salsa::db]
[207](https://docs.rs#207)#[derive(Clone, Default)]
[208](https://docs.rs#208)pub struct RootDatabase {
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    storage: salsa::Storage<Self>,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    files: Files,
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// The project file-set input (lazily created on the first file change). Held outside salsa
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    /// as a handle so `apply_change` can update it.
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    root: Option<SourceRoot>,
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    /// The `project.godot` config input (lazily created on the first config push). Held outside
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    /// salsa as a handle so `apply_change` can update it (M4 autoloads).
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    config: Option<ProjectConfig>,
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    /// A runtime-injected engine model. `None` falls back to the bundled blob on native and to "no
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    /// engine model" on `wasm32` (where nothing is embedded). The wasm binding fetches the blob and
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    /// installs it here via [`RootDatabase::set_engine_api`] (Playbook §4.4). Held outside salsa (a
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    /// process-lifetime `&'static`, leaked once).
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    engine: Option<&'static EngineApi>,
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// The host-level warning-strictness override (CLI `--strict`/`--engine-defaults`). A plain
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    /// field — read only by the non-tracked `type_diagnostics`, never a salsa input.
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    warning_override: WarningOverride,
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// `wasm32`-only: the [`EngineGeneration`] input that makes a *later* `set_engine_api` invalidate
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    /// queries memoized while the model was still absent (so the order "query, then load the engine"
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    /// is correct, not just "load, then query"). Lazily created on the first structural change.
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    engine_gen: Option<EngineGeneration>,
[230](https://docs.rs#230)}
[231](https://docs.rs#231)
[232](https://docs.rs#232)// `salsa::Storage` is not `Debug`, but the public `AnalysisHost`/`Analysis` that will own a
[233](https://docs.rs#233)// `RootDatabase` must stay `Debug` (frozen API); hand-impl an opaque one.
[234](https://docs.rs#234)impl std::fmt::Debug for RootDatabase {
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
[236](https://docs.rs#236)        f.debug_struct("RootDatabase").finish_non_exhaustive()
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    }
[238](https://docs.rs#238)}
[239](https://docs.rs#239)
[240](https://docs.rs#240)impl RootDatabase {
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    /// Create/update `file`'s text input (the single input-mutation primitive `apply_change`
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    /// drives). Clones the `Arc`-backed [`Files`] handle first so `self` is free to pass as the
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    /// `&mut dyn Db` the salsa setter needs.
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    pub fn set_file_text(&mut self, file: FileId, text: &str, durability: Durability) {
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        let files = self.files.clone();
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        files.set_file_text(self, file, text, durability);
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    }
[248](https://docs.rs#248)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    /// Set `file`'s `res://` path (the loader supplies it on add; M3 `preload`/`extends` resolve
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    /// through it). Guarded against no-op re-sets — see [`Files::set_file_path`].
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    pub fn set_file_path(&mut self, file: FileId, path: &str) {
[252](https://docs.rs#252)        let files = self.files.clone();
[253](https://docs.rs#253)        files.set_file_path(self, file, path);
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    }
[255](https://docs.rs#255)
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    /// Remove `file`'s entry from the side table.
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    pub fn remove_file(&mut self, file: FileId) {
[258](https://docs.rs#258)        self.files.remove(file);
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    }
[260](https://docs.rs#260)
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// Set the host-level warning-strictness override (a CLI `--strict`/`--engine-defaults`
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    /// policy). A plain field — changing it does not touch salsa, so it never re-runs inference;
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    /// `type_diagnostics` re-reads it on the next snapshot.
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    pub fn set_warning_override(&mut self, ov: WarningOverride) {
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        self.warning_override = ov;
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    }
[267](https://docs.rs#267)
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    /// Set the project's `project.godot` text (the loader supplies it on project open / when it
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// changes — M4 autoloads). No-op if unchanged: salsa bumps an input field's revision on
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// every set even for an identical value, so a redundant push would needlessly invalidate the
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    /// autoload registry. Held at `MEDIUM` durability, so a `.gd` keystroke never touches it.
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    pub fn set_project_config(&mut self, text: &str) {
[273](https://docs.rs#273)        if let Some(cfg) = self.config {
[274](https://docs.rs#274)            if cfg.project_godot_text(self).as_ref() == text {
[275](https://docs.rs#275)                return;
[276](https://docs.rs#276)            }
[277](https://docs.rs#277)            cfg.set_project_godot_text(self)
[278](https://docs.rs#278)                .with_durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[279](https://docs.rs#279)                .to(Arc::from(text));
[280](https://docs.rs#280)        } else {
[281](https://docs.rs#281)            self.config = Some(
[282](https://docs.rs#282)                ProjectConfig::builder(Arc::from(text))
[283](https://docs.rs#283)                    .durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[284](https://docs.rs#284)                    .new(self),
[285](https://docs.rs#285)            );
[286](https://docs.rs#286)        }
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    }
[288](https://docs.rs#288)
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    /// Install a runtime-loaded engine model (the wasm path: a `fetch`ed `extension_api` blob
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    /// decoded via [`EngineApi::from_bytes`]). Leaked to `&'static` (one per session, process
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    /// lifetime). **Load-once before any query** — the engine model is not a salsa input, so a later
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    /// set would not invalidate cached reads; first-wins (a redundant install is ignored, so the
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    /// leak happens at most once). Native builds normally never call this (they fall back to the
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    /// bundled blob); it is the seam the wasm/wasip1 binding uses.
[295](https://docs.rs#295)    pub fn set_engine_api(&mut self, api: EngineApi) {
[296](https://docs.rs#296)        if self.engine.is_none() {
[297](https://docs.rs#297)            self.engine = Some(Box::leak(Box::new(api)));
[298](https://docs.rs#298)            // wasm: advance the generation so any query memoized while the model was absent (the
[299](https://docs.rs#299)            // "query before load" order) recomputes. Native never reaches here through the bindings,
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            // and its bundled model is present from the start, so it needs no generation tracking.
[301](https://docs.rs#301)            #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
[302](https://docs.rs#302)            self.bump_engine_generation();
[303](https://docs.rs#303)        }
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    }
[305](https://docs.rs#305)
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    /// wasm-only: create-or-advance the [`EngineGeneration`] input (see its docs). Creating it the
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    /// first time is harmless; advancing it invalidates every query that read `engine()`.
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    fn bump_engine_generation(&mut self) {
[310](https://docs.rs#310)        if let Some(eg) = self.engine_gen {
[311](https://docs.rs#311)            let next = eg.generation(self).wrapping_add(1);
[312](https://docs.rs#312)            eg.set_generation(self)
[313](https://docs.rs#313)                .with_durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[314](https://docs.rs#314)                .to(next);
[315](https://docs.rs#315)        } else {
[316](https://docs.rs#316)            self.engine_gen = Some(
[317](https://docs.rs#317)                EngineGeneration::builder(0)
[318](https://docs.rs#318)                    .durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[319](https://docs.rs#319)                    .new(self),
[320](https://docs.rs#320)            );
[321](https://docs.rs#321)        }
[322](https://docs.rs#322)    }
[323](https://docs.rs#323)
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    /// Rebuild the project file-set input from the current side table. Call this from
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    /// `apply_change` **only when a file was added or removed** — never on a body edit — so the
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    /// MEDIUM-durability project input (and everything derived from it) stays stable across
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    /// keystrokes.
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    pub fn sync_source_root(&mut self) {
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        // wasm: ensure the engine generation exists before the first query runs, so every query's
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        // `engine()` read records a dependency on it — otherwise a `set_engine_api` afterwards could
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        // not invalidate a query that ran before the input existed. (The first structural change
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        // always precedes the first query, since the Session early-returns for unknown URIs.)
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        if self.engine_gen.is_none() {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)            self.engine_gen = Some(
[336](https://docs.rs#336)                EngineGeneration::builder(0)
[337](https://docs.rs#337)                    .durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[338](https://docs.rs#338)                    .new(self),
[339](https://docs.rs#339)            );
[340](https://docs.rs#340)        }
[341](https://docs.rs#341)        let files = self.files.all();
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        if let Some(root) = self.root {
[343](https://docs.rs#343)            root.set_files(self)
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                .with_durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                .to(files);
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        } else {
[347](https://docs.rs#347)            // A fresh root starts INCOMPLETE — only the loader's explicit claim
[348](https://docs.rs#348)            // (`set_workspace_complete`) flips it.
[349](https://docs.rs#349)            let root = SourceRoot::builder(files, false)
[350](https://docs.rs#350)                .durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[351](https://docs.rs#351)                .new(self);
[352](https://docs.rs#352)            self.root = Some(root);
[353](https://docs.rs#353)        }
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    }
[355](https://docs.rs#355)
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    /// Record the loader's claim that the current file set is the **whole project** (see
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    /// [`SourceRoot::complete`]). No-op if unchanged (salsa bumps an input field's revision on
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    /// every set, even for an identical value). Creates the (empty) root if none exists yet so
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    /// the claim survives a set-before-first-file ordering.
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    pub fn set_workspace_complete(&mut self, complete: bool) {
[361](https://docs.rs#361)        if let Some(root) = self.root {
[362](https://docs.rs#362)            if root.complete(self) != complete {
[363](https://docs.rs#363)                root.set_complete(self)
[364](https://docs.rs#364)                    .with_durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[365](https://docs.rs#365)                    .to(complete);
[366](https://docs.rs#366)            }
[367](https://docs.rs#367)        } else {
[368](https://docs.rs#368)            let root = SourceRoot::builder(self.files.all(), complete)
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                .durability(Durability::MEDIUM)
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                .new(self);
[371](https://docs.rs#371)            self.root = Some(root);
[372](https://docs.rs#372)        }
[373](https://docs.rs#373)    }
[374](https://docs.rs#374)}

[380](https://docs.rs#380)impl Db for RootDatabase {
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    fn file_text(&self, file: FileId) -> Option<FileText> {
[382](https://docs.rs#382)        self.files.file_text(file)
[383](https://docs.rs#383)    }
[384](https://docs.rs#384)
[385](https://docs.rs#385)    // A runtime-injected model wins; else native falls back to the bundled blob and wasm32 to
[386](https://docs.rs#386)    // `None` (until the binding installs a fetched blob). clippy sees one target per build.
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    #[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)]
[388](https://docs.rs#388)    fn engine(&self) -> Option<&'static EngineApi> {
[389](https://docs.rs#389)        // wasm: record a dependency on the generation so a later `set_engine_api` invalidates this
[390](https://docs.rs#390)        // read. (Native skips this entirely — the bundled model is constant, so zero overhead.)
[391](https://docs.rs#391)        #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
[392](https://docs.rs#392)        if let Some(eg) = self.engine_gen {
[393](https://docs.rs#393)            let _ = eg.generation(self);
[394](https://docs.rs#394)        }
[395](https://docs.rs#395)        if let Some(api) = self.engine {
[396](https://docs.rs#396)            return Some(api);
[397](https://docs.rs#397)        }
[398](https://docs.rs#398)        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
[399](https://docs.rs#399)        {
[400](https://docs.rs#400)            Some(gdscript_api::bundled())
[401](https://docs.rs#401)        }
[402](https://docs.rs#402)        #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
[403](https://docs.rs#403)        {
[404](https://docs.rs#404)            None
[405](https://docs.rs#405)        }
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    }
[407](https://docs.rs#407)
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    fn source_root(&self) -> Option<SourceRoot> {

[426](https://docs.rs#426)    fn parse_query_returns_a_cst() {
[427](https://docs.rs#427)        let mut db = RootDatabase::default();
[428](https://docs.rs#428)        db.set_file_text(FileId(0), "func f():\n\tpass\n", Durability::LOW);
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        let ft = db.file_text(FileId(0)).unwrap();
[430](https://docs.rs#430)        let p = parse(&db, ft);
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        assert!(p.errors().is_empty());
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        // Re-querying the same input returns the memoized value (no re-parse).
[433](https://docs.rs#433)        assert_eq!(parse(&db, ft).debug_tree(), p.debug_tree());
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    }

[436](https://docs.rs#436)    #[test]
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    fn set_get_remove_round_trips() {
[438](https://docs.rs#438)        let mut db = RootDatabase::default();
[439](https://docs.rs#439)        let id = FileId(7);
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        db.set_file_text(id, "var x = 1\n", Durability::LOW);
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        assert_eq!(db.file_text(id).unwrap().text(&db).as_ref(), "var x = 1\n");
[442](https://docs.rs#442)        // Update in place.
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        db.set_file_text(id, "var y = 2\n", Durability::LOW);
[444](https://docs.rs#444)        assert_eq!(db.file_text(id).unwrap().text(&db).as_ref(), "var y = 2\n");
[445](https://docs.rs#445)        // Remove.
[446](https://docs.rs#446)        db.remove_file(id);
[447](https://docs.rs#447)        assert!(db.file_text(id).is_none());
[448](https://docs.rs#448)    }

[450](https://docs.rs#450)    #[test]
[451](https://docs.rs#451)    fn res_path_round_trips_and_guards_no_op_sets() {
[452](https://docs.rs#452)        let mut db = RootDatabase::default();
[453](https://docs.rs#453)        let id = FileId(3);
[454](https://docs.rs#454)        // No path until the loader sets one.
[455](https://docs.rs#455)        db.set_file_text(id, "class_name A\n", Durability::LOW);
[456](https://docs.rs#456)        assert_eq!(db.file_text(id).unwrap().res_path(&db), None);
[457](https://docs.rs#457)        // Set, then read back.
[458](https://docs.rs#458)        db.set_file_path(id, "res://a.gd");
[459](https://docs.rs#459)        assert_eq!(
[460](https://docs.rs#460)            db.file_text(id).unwrap().res_path(&db).as_deref(),
[461](https://docs.rs#461)            Some("res://a.gd")
[462](https://docs.rs#462)        );
[463](https://docs.rs#463)        // A re-set of the SAME path is a guarded no-op (does not panic / regress); a real rename
[464](https://docs.rs#464)        // updates it.
[465](https://docs.rs#465)        db.set_file_path(id, "res://a.gd");
[466](https://docs.rs#466)        db.set_file_path(id, "res://b.gd");
[467](https://docs.rs#467)        assert_eq!(
[468](https://docs.rs#468)            db.file_text(id).unwrap().res_path(&db).as_deref(),
[469](https://docs.rs#469)            Some("res://b.gd")
[470](https://docs.rs#470)        );
[471](https://docs.rs#471)        // Setting a path for an unknown file is a no-op (no panic).
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        db.set_file_path(FileId(999), "res://ghost.gd");
[473](https://docs.rs#473)        assert!(db.file_text(FileId(999)).is_none());
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    }
[475](https://docs.rs#475)}

#### pub fn [set_file_path](https://docs.rs#method.set_file_path)(&self, db: &mut dyn [Db](https://docs.rs/trait.Db.html), file: [FileId](https://docs.rs/gdscript-base/0.5.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_base/struct.FileId.html), path: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

Set `file`’s `res://` path at `MEDIUM` durability (stable project structure, like the
source root). No-op if the file is unknown or the path is unchanged: salsa does **not**
value-backdate an input setter (it bumps the field revision on *every* call, even for an
identical value — verified against salsa 0.27.1 `input.rs:set_field`), so a redundant set
would needlessly invalidate the `res_path_registry`. The guard keeps a re-`apply_change`
of an already-known path free.

# EngineGeneration in gdscript_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.4/gdscript_db/struct.EngineGeneration.html

`pub struct EngineGeneration(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A generation counter that makes the otherwise-untracked runtime engine model **invalidate**
correctly. The engine model is a leaked `&'static` side handle (not a salsa input), so a query
memoized while it was still absent (`engine() == None`, on `wasm32` before `set_engine_api`)
would otherwise return that stale empty result forever. Every `engine()` read records a
dependency on this input; `set_engine_api` bumps it, recomputing those queries. The *value* is
irrelevant — only that setting it advances the revision. Used on `wasm32` only (native has the
bundled model from the start, so it never changes — no generation tracking, no overhead).

# FileText in gdscript_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.4/gdscript_db/struct.FileText.html

`pub struct FileText(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

The VFS leaf: one file’s UTF-8 text, as a salsa input, plus its [ FileId](https://docs.rs/gdscript-base/0.5.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_base/struct.FileId.html) (so a query
holding only a

`FileText` can recover the id for cross-file resolution) and its `res://`
path (so `preload`/`extends "res://…"` resolve to the declaring file — M3).`res_path` is a **separate salsa input field** from `text`: salsa tracks input fields
individually (per-field `revisions`/`durabilities` — verified against salsa 0.27.1
`input.rs`), so a query reading only `res_path` (the `res_path_registry`) *backdates* across
a `text` keystroke — exactly the firewall that protects `file_class_name`. It is held at
`MEDIUM` durability (set on file add, stable across edits); `text` stays `LOW`.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#80)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#80)

The file’s full text (interned `Arc<str>`; the getter returns `&Arc<str>`).

The opaque file id this text belongs to.

The file’s project-relative `res://` path, if the loader supplied one (`None` in
single-file mode / tests — then `preload`/`extends "res://…"` resolve to the seam).

# ProjectConfig in gdscript_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.4/gdscript_db/struct.ProjectConfig.html

`pub struct ProjectConfig(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

The project’s `project.godot`, injected as raw text — the wasm-clean core never reads the
filesystem, so the loader pushes the bytes exactly like a `.gd` file. The autoload index is a
tracked query that parses this text (M4). Held at `MEDIUM` durability (project structure,
stable across `.gd` keystrokes), so a body edit (LOW) never invalidates the autoload registry.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#264-266)#### pub fn [set_warning_override](https://docs.rs#method.set_warning_override)(&mut self, ov: [WarningOverride](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html))

#### pub fn [set_warning_override](https://docs.rs#method.set_warning_override)(&mut self, ov: [WarningOverride](https://docs.rs/enum.WarningOverride.html))

Set the host-level warning-strictness override (a CLI `--strict`/`--engine-defaults`
policy). A plain field — changing it does not touch salsa, so it never re-runs inference;
`type_diagnostics` re-reads it on the next snapshot.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#272-287)#### pub fn [set_project_config](https://docs.rs#method.set_project_config)(&mut self, text: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#272-287)

#### pub fn [set_project_config](https://docs.rs#method.set_project_config)(&mut self, text: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

Set the project’s `project.godot` text (the loader supplies it on project open / when it
changes — M4 autoloads). No-op if unchanged: salsa bumps an input field’s revision on
every set even for an identical value, so a redundant push would needlessly invalidate the
autoload registry. Held at `MEDIUM` durability, so a `.gd` keystroke never touches it.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#295-304)#### pub fn [set_engine_api](https://docs.rs#method.set_engine_api)(&mut self, api: [EngineApi](https://docs.rs/gdscript-api/0.5.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_api/struct.EngineApi.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#295-304)

#### pub fn [set_engine_api](https://docs.rs#method.set_engine_api)(&mut self, api: [EngineApi](https://docs.rs/gdscript-api/0.5.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_api/struct.EngineApi.html))

Install a runtime-loaded engine model (the wasm path: a `fetch`ed `extension_api` blob
decoded via [ EngineApi::from_bytes](https://docs.rs/gdscript-api/0.5.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/gdscript_api/struct.EngineApi.html#method.from_bytes)). Leaked to

`&'static` (one per session, process
lifetime). **Load-once before any query**— the engine model is not a salsa input, so a later set would not invalidate cached reads; first-wins (a redundant install is ignored, so the leak happens at most once). Native builds normally never call this (they fall back to the bundled blob); it is the seam the wasm/wasip1 binding uses.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#328-354)#### pub fn [sync_source_root](https://docs.rs#method.sync_source_root)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#328-354)

#### pub fn [sync_source_root](https://docs.rs#method.sync_source_root)(&mut self)

Rebuild the project file-set input from the current side table. Call this from
`apply_change` **only when a file was added or removed** — never on a body edit — so the
MEDIUM-durability project input (and everything derived from it) stays stable across
keystrokes.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#360-373)#### pub fn [set_workspace_complete](https://docs.rs#method.set_workspace_complete)(&mut self, complete: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Record the loader’s claim that the current file set is the **whole project** (see
[ SourceRoot::complete](https://docs.rs/struct.SourceRoot.html#method.complete)). No-op if unchanged (salsa bumps an input field’s revision on
every set, even for an identical value). Creates the (empty) root if none exists yet so
the claim survives a set-before-first-file ordering.

# SourceRoot in gdscript_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.4/gdscript_db/struct.SourceRoot.html

`pub struct SourceRoot(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

The project’s file set — a salsa input so project-wide queries (the global `class_name`
registry, M1) iterate the files incrementally. It changes only when a file is **added or
removed**, never on a body edit, and is held at MEDIUM durability — so a keystroke (a `LOW`
change) never invalidates project-wide derived data.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#96)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-SourceRoot-1)### impl [SourceRoot](https://docs.rs/struct.SourceRoot.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#96)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-SourceRoot-1)

### impl [SourceRoot](https://docs.rs/struct.SourceRoot.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#96)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/gdscript_db/lib.rs.html#96)

Every file currently in the project, ordered by `FileId` for determinism.

The loader’s assertion that this file set is the **whole project** (every `.gd` under the
project root was fed in). Default `false`. Absence-based diagnostics (`UNDEFINED_FUNCTION`
/ `UNDEFINED_IDENTIFIER`) key on this: proving a name is defined *nowhere* requires seeing
*everywhere*, and neither `source_root().is_some()` (true after one lone file) nor
`project_config().is_some()` (a single-file CLI run still discovers `project.godot`) can
establish that — only the loader knows whether it walked the whole root.

# WarningOverride in gdscript_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-db/0.5.4/gdscript_db/enum.WarningOverride.html

```
pub enum WarningOverride {
    None,
    Strict,
    EngineDefaults,
}
```
## Expand description

The database trait `gdscript-hir` / `gdscript-ide` depend on. `#[salsa::db]` on the *trait*
makes it a salsa supertrait, so any `&dyn Db` upcasts to `&dyn salsa::Database` and every
`#[salsa::tracked]` free function downstream can take `db: &dyn Db`.
A host/CLI-level override of the warning-strictness baseline `type_diagnostics` resolves against
(regardless of `project.godot` presence). A plain (non-salsa) per-session policy knob: it is read
**only** inside the non-tracked `type_diagnostics`, so it never enters the salsa query graph and
cannot break the W1 firewall (a warning-level change must never re-run inference).

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.None)

### None

Auto-select by project presence (the default): standalone ⇒ strict, project ⇒ engine defaults.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Strict)

### Strict

Force the strict baseline (the opt-in group promoted to WARN) even with a `project.godot`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EngineDefaults)

### EngineDefaults

Force Godot’s engine defaults (the opt-in group stays IGNORE) even in standalone mode.

# gdscript-fmt 0.5.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-fmt/0.5.4

# gdscript-fmt

The GDScript source formatter for [ gdscript-analyzer](https://github.com/yanivkalfa/gdscript-analyzer).

A pure `(source, config) -> source` function — no engine model, no filesystem, `wasm32`-safe.
**Safety first:** it normalizes whitespace (indentation → tabs, trailing whitespace, final
newline) by re-emitting every significant token verbatim, and in `safe_mode` (the default) it
re-lexes its own output and **falls back to the original** if the significant token stream
changed — so it can never alter the meaning of your code, even on input it doesn't fully
understand.

```
use ;
let tidy = format;
```
Line-reflow / intra-line spacing (full gdformat parity) is the documented next step; today the formatter normalizes block indentation and line/file whitespace.

# cstree - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cstree/^0.14/

## Expand description

`cstree` is a generic library for creating and working with concrete syntax trees (CSTs).

“Traditional” abstract syntax trees (ASTs) usually contain different types of nodes which
represent different syntactical elements of the source text of a document and reduce its
information to the minimal amount necessary to correctly interpret it. In contrast, CSTs are
lossless representations of the entire input where all tree nodes are represented homogeneously
(i.e., the nodes are *untyped*), but are tagged with a [ RawSyntaxKind](https://docs.rs/struct.RawSyntaxKind.html)  to determine the kind
of grammatical element they represent.

One big advantage of this representation is that it cannot only recreate the original source
exactly, but also lends itself very well to the representation of *incomplete or erroneous*
trees and is thus highly suited for usage in contexts such as IDEs or any other application
where a user is *editing* the source text.

The concept of and the data structures for `cstree`’s syntax trees are inspired in part by
Swift’s [libsyntax](https://github.com/apple/swift/tree/5e2c815edfd758f9b1309ce07bfc01c4bc20ec23/lib/Syntax).
Trees consist of two layers: the inner tree (called *green* tree) contains the actual source
text as position independent green nodes. Tokens and nodes that appear identically at multiple
places in the source are deduplicated in this representation in order to store the tree
efficiently. This means that a green tree may not actually structurally be a tree. To remedy
this, the real syntax tree is constructed on top of the green tree as a secondary tree (called
the *red* tree), which models the exact source structure.
As a possible third layer, a strongly typed AST [can be built](https://docs.rs#ast-layer) on top of the red tree.

The `cstree` implementation is a fork of the excellent [ rowan](https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rowan/),
developed by the authors of

[rust-analyzer](https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rust-analyzer/)who wrote up a conceptual overview of their implementation in

[their repository](https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rust-analyzer/blob/master/docs/dev/syntax.md#trees). Notable differences of

`cstree` compared to `rowan`:- Syntax trees (red trees) are created lazily, but are persistent. Once a red node has been
created by `cstree`, it will remain allocated. In contrast,`rowan`re-creates the red layer on the fly on each traversal of the tree. Apart from the trade-off discussed[here](https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rust-analyzer/blob/master/docs/dev/syntax.md#memoized-rednodes), this helps to achieve good tree traversal speed while helping to provide the following:
- Syntax (red) nodes are `Send`and`Sync`, allowing to share realized trees across threads. This is achieved by atomically reference counting syntax trees as a whole, which also gets rid of the need to reference count individual nodes.
- `SyntaxNode`
- `cstree`trees are trees over interned strings. This means- `cstree`will deduplicate the text of tokens with the same source string, such as identifiers with the same name. In this position,- `rowan`stores each token’s text together with its metadata as a custom DST (dynamically-sized type).
- `cstree`includes some performance optimizations for tree creation: it only allocates space for new nodes on the heap if they are not in cache and avoids recursively hashing subtrees by pre-hashing them.
- `cstree`includes some performance optimizations for tree traversal: persisting red nodes allows tree traversal methods to return references instead of cloning nodes, which involves updating the tree’s reference count. You can still- `clone`the reference to obtain an owned node, but you only pay that cost when you need to.
- The downside of offering thread safe syntax trees is that `cstree`cannot offer any mutability API for its CSTs. Trees can still be updated into new trees through[replacing](https://docs.rs/syntax/struct.SyntaxNode.html#method.replace_with)nodes, but cannot be mutated in place.

[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-feature-flags)Cargo Feature Flags

`cstree` contains several optional features that extend the crate’s functionality.

- `std`(enabled by default) - Support for standard library features
- `derive`- Adds support for deriving the- `Syntax`trait
- `serialize`- Implements- `serde::{De,}Serialize`for CSTs
- `lasso`- Allows using interners from the- `lasso`crate for green trees.- When enabled, `cstree`’s default interners will use`lasso`internally, too.

- When enabled,
- `multi_threaded_interning`- Additionally provide threadsafe interner types.- Where applicable (and if the corresponding features are selected), enabling this feature will also make `cstree`provide compatibility implementations for multi-threaded interners from other crates.
- Enabling this feature will automatically enable the `lasso`feature, as the multi-threaded interners are backed by`lasso`.

- Where applicable (and if the corresponding features are selected), enabling this feature will also make

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting Started

If you’re looking at `cstree`, you’re probably looking at or already writing a parser and are considering using
concrete syntax trees as its output. We’ll talk more about parsing below – first, let’s have a look at what needs
to happen to go from input text to a `cstree` syntax tree:

-
Define an enumeration of the types of tokens (like keywords) and nodes (like “an expression”) that you want to have in your syntax and implement `Syntax`
-
Create a `GreenNodeBuilder``start_node``token``finish_node`
-
Call `SyntaxNode::new_root``SyntaxNode::new_root_with_resolver``GreenNode`

There’s a full [getting started guide](https://docs.rs/getting_started/index.html) that walks through each of the above steps in detail in the documentation for
the `getting_started` module. The walkthrough goes through the necessary steps bit by bit and skips the lexer, but
the full code plus a runnable interpreter for the small walkthrough language are available in the `readme` example.
[Additional examples](https://github.com/domenicquirl/cstree/tree/master/cstree/examples) can be found in the `examples/` folder in the repository.
A good starting point is the `s_expressions` example, which implements a parser for a small S-Expression language
with guiding comments.

# gdscript_fmt - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gdscript-fmt/0.5.4/target-redirect/gdscript_fmt/

## Expand description

`gdscript-fmt` — the GDScript source formatter (Phase-6 Workstream 3).

Internal layer (not a stable API).Depend on[(the public surface); the items here may change between releases.](https://docs.rs/gdscript-ide)`gdscript-ide`

A pure `fn(source, &FmtConfig) -> String`: no engine model, no filesystem, `wasm32`-safe.
It re-emits the lexer/pre-pass token stream, normalizing **block indentation** (to the
configured unit), **trailing whitespace**, and the **final newline** — every *significant*
token (keywords, identifiers, literals — including multi-line strings, which are single tokens)
is emitted **verbatim**, so meaning cannot change.

It also normalizes **intra-line spacing** (Phase-4 increment A): one space around binary
operators / assignments / `->` / `:=`, after `,` and `:` (in type-annotation and dict contexts),
hugged brackets (`f(x, y)`, `[1, 2]`), tight member access (`a.b`), and tight unary `-x`. The
decision is purely local (previous significant token + innermost bracket), and the genuinely
ambiguous contexts — slice colons `arr[a:b]`, and node-path sigils `$Node/Path` / `%Unique`
(where a stray space around `/` would silently change meaning **without** changing the token
sequence) — are left **verbatim** / kept tight by a small node-path state machine.

**Safe by construction.** In `safe_mode` (the default) the formatter (a) refuses to touch a
file with syntax errors, and (b) re-lexes its own output and **falls back to the original** if
the significant token sequence changed. So it never corrupts code, even input it doesn’t fully
understand. The result is idempotent: `format(format(x)) == format(x)`.

It also performs **length-driven line reflow** (Phase-4 increment C): a single-line statement
that exceeds `line_width` and contains a bracketed group is wrapped flat → compact → exploded via
a small `Doc`-IR, matching gdformat and preserving the token sequence. The remaining gdformat
behaviours (magic trailing comma, operator-chain paren injection, quote normalization) are
token-mutating and documented in `DEVIATIONS.md`.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [FmtConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.FmtConfig.html)
- Formatter options. Defaults match the Godot convention (tabs) and keep the safety net on.
- [Range](https://docs.rs/struct.RangeEdit.html)- Edit
- A single whole-line replacement edit produced by `format_range`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [format](https://docs.rs/fn.format.html)
- Format `source`, returning the tidied text. In`safe_mode`(the default) this returns`source`unchanged rather than risk a meaning-changing edit (a syntax error in the input, or output whose significant tokens differ from the input’s).
- [format_](https://docs.rs/fn.format_range.html)- range
- Format only the part of `source`overlapping the byte range`sel`(for editor “format selection” / LSP`textDocument/rangeFormatting`). The whole document is formatted for correct structure and indentation; the result is the**minimal changed line-hunk**that intersects`sel`, or`None`if nothing in the selection’s lines changes. Applying the edit yields the same bytes the whole-file [`format`] would have produced for that region.

[126](https://docs.rs#126)pub fn format(source: &str, config: &FmtConfig) -> String {
[127](https://docs.rs#127)    // A leading byte-order mark is preserved (gdformat keeps it): strip it, format the rest, re-add it.
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    // Otherwise the reflow — which re-emits each statement from its *significant* tokens — would drop
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    // the BOM (a trivia token) when it re-renders the first line.
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    if let Some(rest) = source.strip_prefix('\u{feff}') {
[131](https://docs.rs#131)        return format!("\u{feff}{}", format(rest, config));
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    }
[133](https://docs.rs#133)    if source.contains("\r\n") {
[134](https://docs.rs#134)        let lf = source.replace("\r\n", "\n");
[135](https://docs.rs#135)        return format_lf(&lf, config).replace('\n', "\r\n");
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    }
[137](https://docs.rs#137)    format_lf(source, config)

[163](https://docs.rs#163)    }
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    let src: Vec<&str> = source.split_inclusive('\n').collect();
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    let out: Vec<&str> = formatted.split_inclusive('\n').collect();
[166](https://docs.rs#166)    // Trim the common prefix and suffix lines: the change is the span between them.
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    let mut p = 0;
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    while p < src.len() && p < out.len() && src[p] == out[p] {
[169](https://docs.rs#169)        p += 1;
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    }
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    let mut s = 0;
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    while s < src.len() - p && s < out.len() - p && src[src.len() - 1 - s] == out[out.len() - 1 - s]
[173](https://docs.rs#173)    {
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        s += 1;
[175](https://docs.rs#175)    }
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    let (changed_start, changed_end) = (p, src.len() - s); // source line span [start, end)
[177](https://docs.rs#177)
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    // Byte offset of each source line start (so `starts[i]` is line `i`'s first byte).
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    let mut starts = Vec::with_capacity(src.len() + 1);
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    let mut acc = 0;
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    for l in &src {
[182](https://docs.rs#182)        starts.push(acc);
[183](https://docs.rs#183)        acc += l.len();
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    }
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    starts.push(acc);
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    let line_of = |off: usize| starts.partition_point(|&b| b <= off).saturating_sub(1);
[187](https://docs.rs#187)
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    let last_byte = source.len().saturating_sub(1);
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    let sel_first = line_of(sel.start.min(last_byte));
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    let sel_last = line_of(sel.end.saturating_sub(1).max(sel.start).min(last_byte));
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    if changed_end <= sel_first || changed_start > sel_last {
[192](https://docs.rs#192)        return None; // the selection's lines are unchanged
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    }
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    Some(RangeEdit {
[195](https://docs.rs#195)        range: starts[changed_start]..starts[changed_end],
[196](https://docs.rs#196)        new_text: out[p..out.len() - s].concat(),
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    })
[198](https://docs.rs#198)}
[199](https://docs.rs#199)
[200](https://docs.rs#200)/// `format` working purely in LF (the caller handles CRLF round-tripping).
[201](https://docs.rs#201)fn format_lf(source: &str, config: &FmtConfig) -> String {
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    let input_parses = gdscript_syntax::parse(source).errors().is_empty();
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    // Safe mode: never reformat around a syntax error — we'd risk mis-indenting a mis-parsed block.
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    if config.safe_mode && !input_parses {
[205](https://docs.rs#205)        return source.to_owned();
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    }
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    // Move an inner class's `extends` onto its own body line (`class C extends B:` → `class C:` /
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    // `extends B`), matching gdformat. Self-validating; a no-op when there is no such class.
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    let unextended = split_inner_class_extends(source);
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    let source = unextended.as_deref().unwrap_or(source);
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    // Collapse single-statement lambda bodies, strip redundant grouping parens, then de-inline suite
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    // bodies, so the rest of the pipeline sees a paren-clean, one-statement-per-line tree with inline
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    // lambdas. Each pre-pass self-validates and is a no-op otherwise.
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    let collapsed = if config.collapse_lambdas {
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        collapse_inline_lambdas(source, config)
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    } else {
[217](https://docs.rs#217)        None
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    };
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    let source = collapsed.as_deref().unwrap_or(source);
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    let stripped = if config.strip_parens {
[221](https://docs.rs#221)        strip_outer_parens(source)
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    } else {
[223](https://docs.rs#223)        None
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    };
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    let source = stripped.as_deref().unwrap_or(source);
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    let expanded = if config.expand_inline_blocks {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)        expand_inline_blocks(source, config)
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    } else {
[229](https://docs.rs#229)        None
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    };
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    let source = expanded.as_deref().unwrap_or(source);
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    let mut out = reindent(source, config);
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    if config.insert_blank_lines {
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        // Purely additive (only inserts blank lines), so the significant-token net still holds.
[235](https://docs.rs#235)        out = insert_def_blanks(&out, config);
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    }
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    if config.reflow {
[238](https://docs.rs#238)        // Length-driven wrapping; token-preserving (no trailing comma added).
[239](https://docs.rs#239)        out = reflow(&out, config);
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    }
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    if config.safe_mode {
[242](https://docs.rs#242)        // The safety net is two-layered, because each catches what the other cannot:
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        // (1) meaning-equivalence catches a dropped / reordered / corrupted *token* — while
[244](https://docs.rs#244)        //     normalising away the rewrites the formatter is allowed to make (string-quote style,
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        //     trailing commas);
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        if !meaning_preserved(source, &out) {
[247](https://docs.rs#247)            return source.to_owned();
[248](https://docs.rs#248)        }
[249](https://docs.rs#249)        // (2) a parse-validity recheck catches a meaning-changing *indentation* edit — indentation
[250](https://docs.rs#250)        //     lives entirely in trivia/synthetic layout, so it is invisible to (1). If the input
[251](https://docs.rs#251)        //     parsed clean, the output must too, else we fall back to the verbatim source.
[252](https://docs.rs#252)        if input_parses && !gdscript_syntax::parse(&out).errors().is_empty() {
[253](https://docs.rs#253)            return source.to_owned();
[254](https://docs.rs#254)        }
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    }
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    out
[257](https://docs.rs#257)}
[258](https://docs.rs#258)
[259](https://docs.rs#259)/// gdformat splits an inner class header's `extends` clause onto the first body line
[260](https://docs.rs#260)/// (`class C extends B:` → `class C:` then `\textends B`). Source pre-pass, parse-tree-driven and
[261](https://docs.rs#261)/// self-validating; returns `None` (leave untouched) if it does not parse, has no such class, or the
[262](https://docs.rs#262)/// rewrite changes meaning or fails to parse.
[263](https://docs.rs#263)fn split_inner_class_extends(source: &str) -> Option<String> {
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    let parse = gdscript_syntax::parse(source);
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    if !parse.errors().is_empty() {
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        return None;
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    // (remove_start, remove_end, insert_pos, insert_text)
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    let mut edits: Vec<(usize, usize, usize, String)> = Vec::new();
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    collect_inner_class_extends(&parse.syntax_node(), source, &mut edits);
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    if edits.is_empty() {
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        return None;
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    }
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    // Apply highest-offset edit first so earlier byte spans stay valid.
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    edits.sort_unstable_by_key(|e| std::cmp::Reverse(e.2));
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    let mut out = source.to_owned();
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    for (rs, re, ins_pos, text) in &edits {
[278](https://docs.rs#278)        out.insert_str(*ins_pos, text);
[279](https://docs.rs#279)        out.replace_range(*rs..*re, "");
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    }
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    // This transform deliberately *moves* the `extends` clause (header → body), which the structural
[282](https://docs.rs#282)    // meaning net would flag as a reorder. It only relocates existing tokens, so validate that the
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    // significant-token multiset is unchanged and the result parses clean.
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    if !same_token_multiset(source, &out) || !gdscript_syntax::parse(&out).errors().is_empty() {
[285](https://docs.rs#285)        return None;
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    }
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    Some(out)
[288](https://docs.rs#288)}
[289](https://docs.rs#289)
[290](https://docs.rs#290)/// Whether two sources contain the same multiset of significant (non-trivia) `(kind, text)` tokens —
[291](https://docs.rs#291)/// order-insensitive. Used to validate a transform that only *relocates* existing tokens.
[292](https://docs.rs#292)fn same_token_multiset(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    fn bag(s: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
[294](https://docs.rs#294)        let mut v: Vec<(String, String)> = gdscript_syntax::tokenize(s)
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            .into_iter()
[296](https://docs.rs#296)            .filter(|t| !t.kind.is_trivia() && t.kind != SyntaxKind::Semicolon)
[297](https://docs.rs#297)            .map(|t| (format!("{:?}", t.kind), s[t.range].to_owned()))
[298](https://docs.rs#298)            .collect();
[299](https://docs.rs#299)        v.sort();
[300](https://docs.rs#300)        v
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    }
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    bag(a) == bag(b)
[303](https://docs.rs#303)}
[304](https://docs.rs#304)
[305](https://docs.rs#305)/// Collect the edits that split each inner class's `extends` clause onto its first body line.
[306](https://docs.rs#306)fn collect_inner_class_extends(
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    node: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode,
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    src: &str,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    edits: &mut Vec<(usize, usize, usize, String)>,
[310](https://docs.rs#310)) {
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    for child in node.children() {
[313](https://docs.rs#313)        let edit = (child.kind() == S::InnerClassDecl)
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            .then(|| inner_class_extends_edit(child, src))
[315](https://docs.rs#315)            .flatten();
[316](https://docs.rs#316)        if let Some(edit) = edit {
[317](https://docs.rs#317)            edits.push(edit);
[318](https://docs.rs#318)        }
[319](https://docs.rs#319)        collect_inner_class_extends(child, src, edits);
[320](https://docs.rs#320)    }
[321](https://docs.rs#321)}
[322](https://docs.rs#322)
[323](https://docs.rs#323)/// For an inner class whose header carries `extends T`, build the edit that removes ` extends T` from
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// the header and inserts `<body-indent>extends T\n` before the first body statement. `None` when the
[325](https://docs.rs#325)/// class has no `extends`, no body statement, or any required token is missing.
[326](https://docs.rs#326)fn inner_class_extends_edit(
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    class: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode,
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    src: &str,
[329](https://docs.rs#329)) -> Option<(usize, usize, usize, String)> {
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[331](https://docs.rs#331)    use cstree::util::NodeOrToken;
[332](https://docs.rs#332)    let name = class.children().find(|c| c.kind() == S::Name)?;
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    let body = class.children().find(|c| c.kind() == S::ClassBody)?;
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    // The header tokens (direct children) hold `extends`, the type spelling, and the `:`.
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    let mut extends_start = None;
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    let mut colon_start = None;
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    for c in class.children_with_tokens() {
[338](https://docs.rs#338)        if let NodeOrToken::Token(t) = c {
[339](https://docs.rs#339)            match t.kind() {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)                S::ExtendsKw if extends_start.is_none() => {
[341](https://docs.rs#341)                    extends_start = Some(usize::from(t.text_range().start()));
[342](https://docs.rs#342)                }
[343](https://docs.rs#343)                S::Colon if extends_start.is_some() && colon_start.is_none() => {
[344](https://docs.rs#344)                    colon_start = Some(usize::from(t.text_range().start()));
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                }
[346](https://docs.rs#346)                _ => {}
[347](https://docs.rs#347)            }
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        }
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    }
[350](https://docs.rs#350)    let extends_start = extends_start?;
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    let colon_start = colon_start?;
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    // The type spelling sits between `extends` and `:`.
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    let ty = src.get(extends_start..colon_start)?.trim();
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    let ty = ty.strip_prefix("extends")?.trim();
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    if ty.is_empty() {
[356](https://docs.rs#356)        return None;
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    }
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    // Remove ` extends T` — from the name's end up to the colon (drops the joining space too).
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    let remove_start = usize::from(name.text_range().end());
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    let remove_end = colon_start;
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    // Insert the `extends` line at the first body statement's indentation (its node range starts at
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    // the leading whitespace, so read it forward from there).
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    let first_stmt = body.children().next()?;
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    let stmt_start = usize::from(first_stmt.text_range().start());
[365](https://docs.rs#365)    let indent: String = src[stmt_start..]
[366](https://docs.rs#366)        .chars()
[367](https://docs.rs#367)        .take_while(|&c| c == '\t' || c == ' ')
[368](https://docs.rs#368)        .collect();
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    let insert = format!("{indent}extends {ty}\n");
[370](https://docs.rs#370)    Some((remove_start, remove_end, stmt_start, insert))
[371](https://docs.rs#371)}
[372](https://docs.rs#372)
[373](https://docs.rs#373)/// gdformat moves an inline suite body to its own indented line (`if c: x` → two lines, `func f():
[374](https://docs.rs#374)/// return` → split), while keeping an inline *lambda* body (`func(): x`). We do it as a source
[375](https://docs.rs#375)/// pre-pass driven by the parse tree: find each block whose first statement shares its header's line
[376](https://docs.rs#376)/// — and whose parent is a real statement/declaration, not a `LambdaExpr` — and insert a newline +
[377](https://docs.rs#377)/// indentation before the body. Returns `None` (leave the source untouched) if it does not parse,
[378](https://docs.rs#378)/// nothing is inline, or the rewrite would drop a significant token / fail to parse.
[379](https://docs.rs#379)fn expand_inline_blocks(source: &str, config: &FmtConfig) -> Option<String> {
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    let parse = gdscript_syntax::parse(source);
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    if !parse.errors().is_empty() {
[382](https://docs.rs#382)        return None;
[383](https://docs.rs#383)    }
[384](https://docs.rs#384)    let unit = config.indent_unit();
[385](https://docs.rs#385)    // Each split is `(start, replace_len, text)`: `replace_len` bytes at `start` become `text`.
[386](https://docs.rs#386)    let mut splits: Vec<(usize, usize, String)> = Vec::new();
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    collect_inline_splits(&parse.syntax_node(), source, 0, &unit, &mut splits);
[388](https://docs.rs#388)    if splits.is_empty() {
[389](https://docs.rs#389)        return None;
[390](https://docs.rs#390)    }
[391](https://docs.rs#391)    splits.sort_by_key(|(off, ..)| std::cmp::Reverse(*off)); // apply right-to-left so offsets stay valid
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    let mut out = source.to_owned();
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    for (off, len, text) in &splits {
[394](https://docs.rs#394)        out.replace_range(*off..*off + *len, text);
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    }
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    // The rewrite only adds layout (newlines/indent), so it must keep every significant token and the
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    // structure intact — verified by a token-equality + parse-validity check.
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    if !same_significant_tokens(source, &out) || !gdscript_syntax::parse(&out).errors().is_empty() {
[399](https://docs.rs#399)        return None;
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    }
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    Some(out)
[402](https://docs.rs#402)}
[403](https://docs.rs#403)
[404](https://docs.rs#404)/// Collect `(offset, inserted_text)` for each inline suite body, recursing with `depth` = the
[405](https://docs.rs#405)/// indentation level of `node`'s own line (incremented when descending into a block).
[406](https://docs.rs#406)fn collect_inline_splits(
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    node: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode,
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    src: &str,
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    depth: usize,
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    unit: &str,
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    splits: &mut Vec<(usize, usize, String)>,
[412](https://docs.rs#412)) {
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    use cstree::util::NodeOrToken;
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    for elem in node.children_with_tokens() {
[416](https://docs.rs#416)        let child = match elem {
[417](https://docs.rs#417)            NodeOrToken::Node(n) => n,
[418](https://docs.rs#418)            NodeOrToken::Token(t) => {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)                // A statement-level `;` separates two statements — replace it (and any following
[420](https://docs.rs#420)                // spaces) with a newline + this block's indent so each lands on its own line; a
[421](https://docs.rs#421)                // *trailing* `;` (nothing after it on the line) is dropped.
[422](https://docs.rs#422)                if t.kind() == S::Semicolon {
[423](https://docs.rs#423)                    let r = t.text_range();
[424](https://docs.rs#424)                    let (s, e) = (usize::from(r.start()), usize::from(r.end()));
[425](https://docs.rs#425)                    let trail = src[e..].len() - src[e..].trim_start_matches([' ', '\t']).len();
[426](https://docs.rs#426)                    let rest = &src[e + trail..];
[427](https://docs.rs#427)                    let text = if rest.starts_with('\n') || rest.is_empty() {
[428](https://docs.rs#428)                        String::new()
[429](https://docs.rs#429)                    } else {
[430](https://docs.rs#430)                        format!("\n{}", unit.repeat(depth))
[431](https://docs.rs#431)                    };
[432](https://docs.rs#432)                    splits.push((s, e + trail - s, text));
[433](https://docs.rs#433)                }
[434](https://docs.rs#434)                continue;
[435](https://docs.rs#435)            }
[436](https://docs.rs#436)        };
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        // A block-introducing child: a statement/declaration `Block` or a property body
[438](https://docs.rs#438)        // (`var x: T: set = f`). Its *inline-body split* (moving the body onto its own indented line)
[439](https://docs.rs#439)        // is skipped for a `LambdaExpr`'s block — a lambda's body stays inline; the wrapper owns its
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        // multi-line layout — but the block still counts as a depth increment so any `;`-separated
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        // statements *inside* the lambda body land at the correct indentation.
[442](https://docs.rs#442)        let is_block = matches!(child.kind(), S::Block | S::PropertyBody);
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        let suite = is_block && node.kind() != S::LambdaExpr;
[444](https://docs.rs#444)        if suite {
[445](https://docs.rs#445)            // The body offset: a `Block`'s first token, or — for a property body, whose own first
[446](https://docs.rs#446)            // token is the `:` — its first getter/setter node (the content after the `:`).
[447](https://docs.rs#447)            let body_offset = if child.kind() == S::PropertyBody {
[448](https://docs.rs#448)                child.children().next().and_then(first_sig_offset)
[449](https://docs.rs#449)            } else {
[450](https://docs.rs#450)                first_sig_offset(child)
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            };
[452](https://docs.rs#452)            let inline_body =
[453](https://docs.rs#453)                body_offset.filter(|&bs| src[..bs].trim_end_matches([' ', '\t']).ends_with(':'));
[454](https://docs.rs#454)            if let Some(bs) = inline_body {
[455](https://docs.rs#455)                splits.push((bs, 0, format!("\n{}", unit.repeat(depth + 1))));
[456](https://docs.rs#456)            }
[457](https://docs.rs#457)        }
[458](https://docs.rs#458)        // A child is one indent level deeper when it is a suite, an inner class's `ClassBody` (whose
[459](https://docs.rs#459)        // members sit a level below the `class` header), or a `match` arm (arms sit a level below the
[460](https://docs.rs#460)        // `match` with no intervening `Block` node).
[461](https://docs.rs#461)        let deeper = is_block
[462](https://docs.rs#462)            || child.kind() == S::ClassBody
[463](https://docs.rs#463)            || (node.kind() == S::MatchStmt && child.kind() == S::MatchArm);
[464](https://docs.rs#464)        collect_inline_splits(child, src, depth + usize::from(deeper), unit, splits);
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    }
[466](https://docs.rs#466)}
[467](https://docs.rs#467)
[468](https://docs.rs#468)/// Collapse a multi-line lambda whose body is a single simple statement onto one line, matching
[469](https://docs.rs#469)/// gdformat (`func():\n\tbody` → `func(): body`), so the surrounding statement can re-flow. Restricted
[470](https://docs.rs#470)/// to a body that is a single statement, not a compound (`if`/`for`/…), on a single physical line, with
[471](https://docs.rs#471)/// only whitespace between the lambda's `:` and the body — so the join is a pure newline/indent removal.
[472](https://docs.rs#472)/// Returns `None` (leave the source) if nothing collapses or the result is not meaning-equivalent.
[473](https://docs.rs#473)fn collapse_inline_lambdas(source: &str, config: &FmtConfig) -> Option<String> {
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    let parse = gdscript_syntax::parse(source);
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    if !parse.errors().is_empty() {
[476](https://docs.rs#476)        return None;
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    }
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    let mut edits: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new(); // (start, end) byte ranges to replace with " "
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    collect_lambda_collapses(&parse.syntax_node(), source, config, &mut edits);
[480](https://docs.rs#480)    if edits.is_empty() {
[481](https://docs.rs#481)        return None;
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    }
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    edits.sort_unstable_by_key(|(s, _)| std::cmp::Reverse(*s));
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    let mut out = source.to_owned();
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    for (s, e) in &edits {
[486](https://docs.rs#486)        out.replace_range(*s..*e, " ");
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    }
[488](https://docs.rs#488)    if !meaning_preserved(source, &out) || !gdscript_syntax::parse(&out).errors().is_empty() {
[489](https://docs.rs#489)        return None;
[490](https://docs.rs#490)    }
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    Some(out)
[492](https://docs.rs#492)}
[493](https://docs.rs#493)
[494](https://docs.rs#494)/// Collect `(start, end)` ranges (the whitespace/newline between a collapsible lambda's `:` and its
[495](https://docs.rs#495)/// body) to replace with a single space.
[496](https://docs.rs#496)fn collect_lambda_collapses(
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    node: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode,
[498](https://docs.rs#498)    src: &str,
[499](https://docs.rs#499)    config: &FmtConfig,
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    edits: &mut Vec<(usize, usize)>,
[501](https://docs.rs#501)) {
[502](https://docs.rs#502)    for child in node.children() {
[503](https://docs.rs#503)        let collapse = (child.kind() == SyntaxKind::LambdaExpr)
[504](https://docs.rs#504)            .then(|| lambda_collapse_range(child, src, config))
[505](https://docs.rs#505)            .flatten();
[506](https://docs.rs#506)        if let Some((s, e)) = collapse {
[507](https://docs.rs#507)            edits.push((s, e));
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        }
[509](https://docs.rs#509)        collect_lambda_collapses(child, src, config, edits);
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    }
[511](https://docs.rs#511)}
[512](https://docs.rs#512)
[513](https://docs.rs#513)/// The byte range between a lambda's `:` and its body to collapse, when the body is a single simple
[514](https://docs.rs#514)/// statement spanning one physical line, the gap is whitespace only (no comment), and the *enclosing*
[515](https://docs.rs#515)/// statement would fit on one line once collapsed (gdformat keeps a lambda multi-line otherwise).
[516](https://docs.rs#516)fn lambda_collapse_range(
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    lambda: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode,
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    src: &str,
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    config: &FmtConfig,
[520](https://docs.rs#520)) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
[521](https://docs.rs#521)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    let block = lambda.children().find(|c| c.kind() == S::Block)?;
[523](https://docs.rs#523)    let stmts: Vec<_> = block.children().collect(); // a block's child nodes are all statements
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    let [stmt] = stmts.as_slice() else {
[525](https://docs.rs#525)        return None;
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    };
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    // A compound body (`func(): if c: …`) stays multi-line, as does a body that itself spans lines.
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    if matches!(
[529](https://docs.rs#529)        stmt.kind(),
[530](https://docs.rs#530)        S::IfStmt | S::ElifClause | S::ElseClause | S::ForStmt | S::WhileStmt | S::MatchStmt
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    ) {
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        return None;
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    }
[534](https://docs.rs#534)    let bs = first_sig_offset(stmt)?; // skip the body's own leading indentation
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    let be = usize::from(stmt.text_range().end());
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    if src[bs..be].contains('\n') {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        return None; // body wrapped over lines — leave it
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    }
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    let pre = src[..bs].trim_end_matches([' ', '\t', '\n', '\r']);
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    if !pre.ends_with(':') {
[541](https://docs.rs#541)        return None;
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    }
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    let gap = &src[pre.len()..bs];
[544](https://docs.rs#544)    if !gap.contains('\n') || gap.contains('#') {
[545](https://docs.rs#545)        return None; // already inline, or a comment sits in the gap
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    }
[547](https://docs.rs#547)    // gdformat only inlines a lambda when the *enclosing* statement then fits on one line; otherwise it
[548](https://docs.rs#548)    // keeps the lambda multi-line. Estimate the collapsed length of the enclosing top-level statement
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    // (the ancestor directly inside a `Block`): its content with every whitespace run squeezed to one
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    // space, plus its indentation. (The estimate matches our canonical spacing closely enough to decide.)
[551](https://docs.rs#551)    let mut top = lambda.clone();
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    while let Some(p) = top.parent() {
[553](https://docs.rs#553)        if p.kind() == S::Block {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)            break;
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        }
[556](https://docs.rs#556)        top = p.clone();
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    }
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    let r = top.text_range();
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    let (ts, te) = (usize::from(r.start()), usize::from(r.end()));
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    let indent_cols = src[..ts]
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        .bytes()
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        .rev()
[563](https://docs.rs#563)        .take_while(|&b| b == b'\t' || b == b' ')
[564](https://docs.rs#564)        .map(|b| if b == b'\t' { 4 } else { 1 })
[565](https://docs.rs#565)        .sum::<usize>();
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    let content: usize = src[ts..te].split_whitespace().map(str::len).sum::<usize>()
[567](https://docs.rs#567)        + src[ts..te].split_whitespace().count().saturating_sub(1); // joined by single spaces
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    if indent_cols + content > config.line_width {
[569](https://docs.rs#569)        return None;
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    }
[571](https://docs.rs#571)    Some((pre.len(), bs))
[572](https://docs.rs#572)}
[573](https://docs.rs#573)
[574](https://docs.rs#574)/// Remove redundant grouping parens from standalone-expression positions, matching gdformat's
[575](https://docs.rs#575)/// `remove_outer_parentheses`. A `ParenExpr` is redundant when its parent uses it as a *whole
[576](https://docs.rs#576)/// expression* (a value / condition / iterable / argument / element / nested paren) rather than as an
[577](https://docs.rs#577)/// *operand* of a larger expression — `(a + b) * c` keeps its parens because the parent is the `*`
[578](https://docs.rs#578)/// `BinExpr`. Returns `None` (leave the source) if it does not parse, has no such parens, or the
[579](https://docs.rs#579)/// result is not meaning-equivalent / does not parse (the net catches a precedence-changing strip).
[580](https://docs.rs#580)fn strip_outer_parens(source: &str) -> Option<String> {
[581](https://docs.rs#581)    let parse = gdscript_syntax::parse(source);
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    if !parse.errors().is_empty() {
[583](https://docs.rs#583)        return None;
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    }
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    let mut dels: Vec<usize> = Vec::new(); // byte offsets of `(`/`)` tokens to delete (1 byte each)
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    collect_redundant_parens(&parse.syntax_node(), &mut dels);
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    collect_empty_signal_parens(&parse.syntax_node(), &mut dels);
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    if dels.is_empty() {
[589](https://docs.rs#589)        return None;
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    }
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    dels.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.cmp(a)); // delete right-to-left
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    let mut out = source.to_owned();
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    for off in &dels {
[594](https://docs.rs#594)        out.replace_range(*off..=*off, "");
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    }
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    if !meaning_preserved(source, &out) || !gdscript_syntax::parse(&out).errors().is_empty() {
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        return None;
[598](https://docs.rs#598)    }
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    Some(out)
[600](https://docs.rs#600)}
[601](https://docs.rs#601)
[602](https://docs.rs#602)/// Whether a `ParenExpr` child of a node of `parent` is a redundant grouping paren (a standalone
[603](https://docs.rs#603)/// expression), not a precedence-bearing operand.
[604](https://docs.rs#604)fn paren_parent_strips(parent: SyntaxKind) -> bool {
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    matches!(
[607](https://docs.rs#607)        parent,
[608](https://docs.rs#608)        S::VarDecl
[609](https://docs.rs#609)            | S::ConstDecl
[610](https://docs.rs#610)            | S::ReturnStmt
[611](https://docs.rs#611)            | S::ForStmt
[612](https://docs.rs#612)            | S::IfStmt
[613](https://docs.rs#613)            | S::ElifClause
[614](https://docs.rs#614)            | S::WhileStmt
[615](https://docs.rs#615)            | S::MatchStmt
[616](https://docs.rs#616)            | S::ExprStmt
[617](https://docs.rs#617)            | S::ArgList
[618](https://docs.rs#618)            | S::ArrayLit
[619](https://docs.rs#619)            | S::DictEntry
[620](https://docs.rs#620)            | S::ParenExpr
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    )
[622](https://docs.rs#622)}
[623](https://docs.rs#623)
[624](https://docs.rs#624)/// Collect the byte offsets of the `(`/`)` tokens of every redundant `ParenExpr`.
[625](https://docs.rs#625)fn collect_redundant_parens(node: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode, dels: &mut Vec<usize>) {
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    use cstree::util::NodeOrToken;
[627](https://docs.rs#627)    for child in node.children() {
[628](https://docs.rs#628)        if child.kind() == SyntaxKind::ParenExpr && paren_parent_strips(node.kind()) {
[629](https://docs.rs#629)            for c in child.children_with_tokens() {
[630](https://docs.rs#630)                let NodeOrToken::Token(t) = c else { continue };
[631](https://docs.rs#631)                if matches!(t.kind(), SyntaxKind::LParen | SyntaxKind::RParen) {
[632](https://docs.rs#632)                    dels.push(usize::from(t.text_range().start()));
[633](https://docs.rs#633)                }
[634](https://docs.rs#634)            }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)        }
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        collect_redundant_parens(child, dels);
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    }
[638](https://docs.rs#638)}
[639](https://docs.rs#639)
[640](https://docs.rs#640)/// Collect the `(`/`)` of a signal's *empty* parameter list — gdformat writes `signal s` not
[641](https://docs.rs#641)/// `signal s()`. (A `func` always keeps its `()`, so this is restricted to signals.)
[642](https://docs.rs#642)fn collect_empty_signal_parens(node: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode, dels: &mut Vec<usize>) {
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    use cstree::util::NodeOrToken;
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    for child in node.children() {
[645](https://docs.rs#645)        let empty_params = (child.kind() == SyntaxKind::SignalDecl)
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            .then(|| child.children().find(|c| c.kind() == SyntaxKind::ParamList))
[647](https://docs.rs#647)            .flatten()
[648](https://docs.rs#648)            .filter(|p| p.children().next().is_none());
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        if let Some(params) = empty_params {
[650](https://docs.rs#650)            for c in params.children_with_tokens() {
[651](https://docs.rs#651)                let NodeOrToken::Token(t) = c else { continue };
[652](https://docs.rs#652)                if matches!(t.kind(), SyntaxKind::LParen | SyntaxKind::RParen) {
[653](https://docs.rs#653)                    dels.push(usize::from(t.text_range().start()));
[654](https://docs.rs#654)                }
[655](https://docs.rs#655)            }
[656](https://docs.rs#656)        }
[657](https://docs.rs#657)        collect_empty_signal_parens(child, dels);
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    }

[660](https://docs.rs#660)
[661](https://docs.rs#661)/// The byte offset of the first significant (non-trivia, non-synthetic) token within `node`.
[662](https://docs.rs#662)fn first_sig_offset(node: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode) -> Option<usize> {
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    use cstree::util::NodeOrToken;
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    for c in node.children_with_tokens() {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)        match c {
[666](https://docs.rs#666)            NodeOrToken::Token(t) => {
[667](https://docs.rs#667)                let k = t.kind();
[668](https://docs.rs#668)                if !k.is_trivia() && !k.is_synthetic_layout() {
