[669](https://docs.rs#669)                    return Some(usize::from(t.text_range().start()));
[670](https://docs.rs#670)                }
[671](https://docs.rs#671)            }
[672](https://docs.rs#672)            NodeOrToken::Node(n) => {
[673](https://docs.rs#673)                if let Some(o) = first_sig_offset(n) {
[674](https://docs.rs#674)                    return Some(o);
[675](https://docs.rs#675)                }
[676](https://docs.rs#676)            }
[677](https://docs.rs#677)        }
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    }
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    None
[680](https://docs.rs#680)}
[681](https://docs.rs#681)
[682](https://docs.rs#682)/// Inter-token spacing: how to join two adjacent significant tokens on one logical line.
[683](https://docs.rs#683)#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
[684](https://docs.rs#684)enum Spacing {
[685](https://docs.rs#685)    /// Tight — no space (`a.b`, `f(`, before `,`/`)`).
[686](https://docs.rs#686)    None,
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    /// Exactly one space (` + `, `, ` after a comma, ` = `).
[688](https://docs.rs#688)    Single,
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    /// Keep the original inter-token whitespace — the ambiguous contexts we refuse to normalize
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    /// (a slice colon `arr[a:b]`). Emits nothing when there was no original whitespace.
[691](https://docs.rs#691)    Verbatim,
[692](https://docs.rs#692)}
[693](https://docs.rs#693)
[694](https://docs.rs#694)/// A value-completing token: a following `+`/`-`/`~` is **binary** (not unary), and a following
[695](https://docs.rs#695)/// `(`/`[` is a **call**/**subscript** (not a grouping paren / array literal).
[696](https://docs.rs#696)fn is_operand_end(k: SyntaxKind) -> bool {
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    matches!(
[699](https://docs.rs#699)        k,
[700](https://docs.rs#700)        S::Int
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            | S::Float
[702](https://docs.rs#702)            | S::String
[703](https://docs.rs#703)            | S::StringName
[704](https://docs.rs#704)            | S::NodePath
[705](https://docs.rs#705)            | S::Ident
[706](https://docs.rs#706)            | S::True
[707](https://docs.rs#707)            | S::False
[708](https://docs.rs#708)            | S::Null
[709](https://docs.rs#709)            | S::ConstPi
[710](https://docs.rs#710)            | S::ConstTau
[711](https://docs.rs#711)            | S::ConstInf
[712](https://docs.rs#712)            | S::ConstNan
[713](https://docs.rs#713)            | S::SelfKw
[714](https://docs.rs#714)            | S::SuperKw
[715](https://docs.rs#715)            | S::RParen
[716](https://docs.rs#716)            | S::RBrack
[717](https://docs.rs#717)            | S::RBrace
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    )
[719](https://docs.rs#719)}
[720](https://docs.rs#720)
[721](https://docs.rs#721)fn is_open_bracket(k: SyntaxKind) -> bool {
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    matches!(
[723](https://docs.rs#723)        k,
[724](https://docs.rs#724)        SyntaxKind::LParen | SyntaxKind::LBrack | SyntaxKind::LBrace
[725](https://docs.rs#725)    )
[726](https://docs.rs#726)}
[727](https://docs.rs#727)
[728](https://docs.rs#728)fn is_close_bracket(k: SyntaxKind) -> bool {
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    matches!(
[730](https://docs.rs#730)        k,
[731](https://docs.rs#731)        SyntaxKind::RParen | SyntaxKind::RBrack | SyntaxKind::RBrace
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    )
[733](https://docs.rs#733)}
[734](https://docs.rs#734)
[735](https://docs.rs#735)/// The spacing to insert *before* `cur`, given the previous significant token `prev` on the same
[736](https://docs.rs#736)/// logical line, the innermost open-bracket kind `top`, and whether `prev` was a **unary** prefix
[737](https://docs.rs#737)/// operator. Node-path runs (`$Node/Path`, `%Unique`) are forced tight by the caller and never
[738](https://docs.rs#738)/// reach here, so a bare `Slash`/`Percent` here is always division/modulo.
[739](https://docs.rs#739)fn space_before(
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    prev: SyntaxKind,
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    cur: SyntaxKind,
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    top: Option<SyntaxKind>,
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    prev_unary: bool,
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    top_enum: bool,
[745](https://docs.rs#745)) -> Spacing {
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[747](https://docs.rs#747)    // An enum body is spaced inside (`{ A, B }`) — unlike a dict (`{"k": v}`) — but an empty `{}`
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    // stays tight. This overrides the bracket-hug rule below for the enum braces only.
[749](https://docs.rs#749)    if top_enum {
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        if prev == S::LBrace && cur != S::RBrace {
[751](https://docs.rs#751)            return Spacing::Single;
[752](https://docs.rs#752)        }
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        if cur == S::RBrace && prev != S::LBrace {
[754](https://docs.rs#754)            return Spacing::Single;
[755](https://docs.rs#755)        }
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    }
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    // --- tight-forcing rules (these carve out every no-space case; the default is one space) ---
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    // Hug the inside of brackets: `(x`, `x)`, `[1`, `1]`, `{k`, `v}`.
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    if is_open_bracket(prev) || is_close_bracket(cur) {
[760](https://docs.rs#760)        return Spacing::None;
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    }
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    // Member access is tight both sides (`.5` / `1.0` are single Float tokens, so a bare `Dot` is
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    // always member access).
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    if cur == S::Dot || prev == S::Dot {
[765](https://docs.rs#765)        return Spacing::None;
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    }
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    // No space before a separator; `@export` is tight after the `@`.
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    if cur == S::Comma || cur == S::Semicolon || prev == S::At {
[769](https://docs.rs#769)        return Spacing::None;
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    }
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    // Tight after a unary prefix operator: `-x`, `+x`, `~x`, `!x`.
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    if prev == S::Tilde || prev == S::Bang || ((prev == S::Minus || prev == S::Plus) && prev_unary)
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    {
[774](https://docs.rs#774)        return Spacing::None;
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    }
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    // Colon: never a space *before* it; *after* it, a dict/type-annotation colon gets one space,
[777](https://docs.rs#777)    // while a slice colon inside `[ ]` is left verbatim (a subscript and a slice are not
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    // distinguishable from local context). `:=` is its own token, handled by the default.
[779](https://docs.rs#779)    if cur == S::Colon {
[780](https://docs.rs#780)        return if top == Some(S::LBrack) {
[781](https://docs.rs#781)            Spacing::Verbatim
[782](https://docs.rs#782)        } else {
[783](https://docs.rs#783)            Spacing::None
[784](https://docs.rs#784)        };
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    }
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    if prev == S::Colon {
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        return if top == Some(S::LBrack) {
[788](https://docs.rs#788)            Spacing::Verbatim
[789](https://docs.rs#789)        } else {
[790](https://docs.rs#790)            Spacing::Single
[791](https://docs.rs#791)        };
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    }
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    // After a separator: one space (`a, b`).
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    if prev == S::Comma || prev == S::Semicolon {
[795](https://docs.rs#795)        return Spacing::Single;
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    }
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    // Open paren: a call hugs an operand callee (`f(`, `a.b(`, `preload(`, `assert(`), and a lambda
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    // header hugs its `func` (`func(x):` — a bare `func(` is always a lambda; a named func has
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    // `func name(`). A grouping paren after a value-keyword keeps its space (`return (x)`, `if (c)`).
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    if cur == S::LParen {
[801](https://docs.rs#801)        return if is_operand_end(prev)
[802](https://docs.rs#802)            || prev == S::PreloadKw
[803](https://docs.rs#803)            || prev == S::AssertKw
[804](https://docs.rs#804)            || prev == S::FuncKw
[805](https://docs.rs#805)        {
[806](https://docs.rs#806)            Spacing::None
[807](https://docs.rs#807)        } else {
[808](https://docs.rs#808)            Spacing::Single
[809](https://docs.rs#809)        };
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    }
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    // Open bracket: a subscript / typed-collection hugs an operand (`arr[i]`, `Array[int]`); an
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    // array literal after an operator/keyword/`,` is spaced.
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    if cur == S::LBrack {
[814](https://docs.rs#814)        return if is_operand_end(prev) {
[815](https://docs.rs#815)            Spacing::None
[816](https://docs.rs#816)        } else {
[817](https://docs.rs#817)            Spacing::Single
[818](https://docs.rs#818)        };
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    }
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    // Everything else — binary/keyword operators, assignments, `->`, `:=`, `{`, atoms, words, and a
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    // unary prefix *before* its operand — takes exactly one space.
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    Spacing::Single
[823](https://docs.rs#823)}
[824](https://docs.rs#824)
[825](https://docs.rs#825)/// Emit a logical-line break: a real `\n` for a content line, or — when collapsing blank lines —
[826](https://docs.rs#826)/// buffer a blank line into `pending_blanks` (flushed, capped, before the next content line).
[827](https://docs.rs#827)fn emit_break(
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    out: &mut String,
[829](https://docs.rs#829)    collapse_on: bool,
[830](https://docs.rs#830)    line_had_content: &mut bool,
[831](https://docs.rs#831)    pending_blanks: &mut usize,
[832](https://docs.rs#832)) {
[833](https://docs.rs#833)    if collapse_on && !*line_had_content {
[834](https://docs.rs#834)        *pending_blanks += 1; // a blank line — capped + flushed when the next content line starts.
[835](https://docs.rs#835)    } else {
[836](https://docs.rs#836)        out.push('\n');
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    }
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    *line_had_content = false;
[839](https://docs.rs#839)}
[840](https://docs.rs#840)
[841](https://docs.rs#841)/// The depth and leading-indentation length of the next code line after token index `idx` (skipping
[842](https://docs.rs#842)/// comment / blank lines), given the current raw depth `cur`. Used to place a block-boundary comment.
[843](https://docs.rs#843)fn next_code_info(toks: &[gdscript_syntax::RawToken], idx: usize, cur: usize) -> (usize, usize) {
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    let mut delta: i32 = 0;
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    let mut indent_len = 0usize;
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    for t in &toks[idx + 1..] {
[848](https://docs.rs#848)        match t.kind {
[849](https://docs.rs#849)            S::Indent => delta += 1,
[850](https://docs.rs#850)            S::Dedent => delta -= 1,
[851](https://docs.rs#851)            S::NewlinePhys | S::Newline => indent_len = 0,
[852](https://docs.rs#852)            S::Whitespace => indent_len = usize::from(t.range.len()),
[853](https://docs.rs#853)            k if k.is_trivia() => {} // comments / line-continuation / BOM
[854](https://docs.rs#854)            _ => {
[855](https://docs.rs#855)                let d = usize::try_from(i32::try_from(cur).unwrap_or(0) + delta).unwrap_or(0);
[856](https://docs.rs#856)                return (d, indent_len);
[857](https://docs.rs#857)            }
[858](https://docs.rs#858)        }
[859](https://docs.rs#859)    }
[860](https://docs.rs#860)    (cur, 0)
[861](https://docs.rs#861)}
[862](https://docs.rs#862)
[863](https://docs.rs#863)/// The intended depth of a block-boundary comment, matching gdformat's
[864](https://docs.rs#864)/// `reconstruct_blank_lines_in_range`: a standalone comment joins the deepest block whose line-range
[865](https://docs.rs#865)/// contains it, which is its own authored indentation level *clamped down* to the deepest open block
[866](https://docs.rs#866)/// around it. `comment_levels` is the comment's authored indentation measured in indent units; the
[867](https://docs.rs#867)/// deepest open block is the deeper of the previous code line's depth (`prev_depth`) and the next
[868](https://docs.rs#868)/// code line's (`next_depth`) — the next statement can reveal a block the prepass has not yet opened
[869](https://docs.rs#869)/// with an `Indent` (a comment that is the first line of a body). So an under-indented comment keeps
[870](https://docs.rs#870)/// its own (shallower) level, while an over-indented one snaps to the deepest real block. A column-0
[871](https://docs.rs#871)/// `#` comment is special-cased by the caller (kept at column 0).
[872](https://docs.rs#872)fn comment_depth(comment_levels: usize, prev_depth: usize, next_depth: usize) -> usize {
[873](https://docs.rs#873)    comment_levels.min(prev_depth.max(next_depth))
[874](https://docs.rs#874)}
[875](https://docs.rs#875)
[876](https://docs.rs#876)/// Re-emit the pre-pass token stream with normalized **indentation**, **intra-line spacing** (when
[877](https://docs.rs#877)/// `config.normalize_spacing`), trailing whitespace, and a single final newline. Significant token
[878](https://docs.rs#878)/// *text* is always emitted verbatim (so meaning is preserved); only the whitespace *between*
[879](https://docs.rs#879)/// tokens — and a logical line's leading indentation — is rewritten. Bracketed-continuation
[880](https://docs.rs#880)/// interiors and node-path runs are kept verbatim / tight (see the module docs).
[881](https://docs.rs#881)#[allow(
[882](https://docs.rs#882)    clippy::too_many_lines,
[883](https://docs.rs#883)    reason = "one cohesive token-stream state machine; the indentation, spacing, bracket-stack and node-path transitions are interdependent and clearer kept together than split across helpers"
[884](https://docs.rs#884))]
[885](https://docs.rs#885)fn reindent(source: &str, config: &FmtConfig) -> String {
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    let raw = gdscript_syntax::tokenize(source);
[887](https://docs.rs#887)    let (toks, _diags) = gdscript_syntax::run_prepass(&raw, source);
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    let unit = config.indent_unit();
[889](https://docs.rs#889)    let spacing_on = config.normalize_spacing;
[890](https://docs.rs#890)    let collapse_on = config.collapse_blank_lines;
[891](https://docs.rs#891)
[892](https://docs.rs#892)    let mut out = String::with_capacity(source.len() + 16);
[893](https://docs.rs#893)    let mut depth: usize = 0;
[894](https://docs.rs#894)    // --- blank-line state (only used when `collapse_on`) ---
[895](https://docs.rs#895)    // Blank lines are buffered, not emitted, until the next content line: we then flush at most
[896](https://docs.rs#896)    // `cap` of them (2 at top level, 1 nested) — knowing the *next* line's depth, since the prepass
[897](https://docs.rs#897)    // emits the `Dedent` between a block and a following top-level line AFTER the blank lines.
[898](https://docs.rs#898)    let mut pending_blanks: usize = 0;
[899](https://docs.rs#899)    // Whether the current logical line emitted any content (a significant token or a comment) — a
[900](https://docs.rs#900)    // line that did not is a blank line.
[901](https://docs.rs#901)    let mut line_had_content = false;
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    // Whether any content has been emitted yet (leading blank lines are stripped entirely).
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    let mut seen_content = false;
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    // `true` at the start of a logical line, before its first significant token (when we re-emit
[905](https://docs.rs#905)    // the indentation, `depth` being final by then).
[906](https://docs.rs#906)    let mut line_start = true;
[907](https://docs.rs#907)    // A synthetic `Newline` precedes the `NewlinePhys` carrying the line's bytes; this swallows that
[908](https://docs.rs#908)    // one `NewlinePhys` so the break is emitted once. See the original notes below.
[909](https://docs.rs#909)    let mut just_broke = false;
[910](https://docs.rs#910)    // Innermost-first stack of open-bracket kinds: `.len()` is the old `bracket_depth` (drives the
[911](https://docs.rs#911)    // continuation logic), `.last()` is the colon-context discriminator for spacing.
[912](https://docs.rs#912)    let mut stack: Vec<SyntaxKind> = Vec::new();
[913](https://docs.rs#913)    // Parallel to the `{` entries in `stack`: whether each brace is an **enum body** (spaced inside,
[914](https://docs.rs#914)    // `{ A, B }`) rather than a dict (tight, `{"k": v}`). `pending_enum` is armed by an `enum` keyword
[915](https://docs.rs#915)    // and consumed by the brace it opens.
[916](https://docs.rs#916)    let mut brace_is_enum: Vec<bool> = Vec::new();
[917](https://docs.rs#917)    let mut pending_enum = false;
[918](https://docs.rs#918)    // --- intra-line spacing state (all reset at a logical-line break) ---
[919](https://docs.rs#919)    let mut prev_sig: Option<SyntaxKind> = None;
[920](https://docs.rs#920)    let mut prev_unary = false;
[921](https://docs.rs#921)    let mut node_path = false;
[922](https://docs.rs#922)    // Original inter-token whitespace, buffered so the next token can keep it (`Verbatim`) or drop
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    // it (and re-synthesize). Only used when `spacing_on`.
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    let mut pending_ws: Option<&str> = None;
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    // Set after a physical newline *inside* brackets: the next line's leading whitespace (alignment)
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    // is kept verbatim — increment A does not reflow bracketed continuations.
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    let mut cont_line_start = false;
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    // The leading whitespace of the current logical line (used to recover a *comment*'s authored
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    // indentation, since the prepass attributes a block-boundary comment to the wrong raw `depth`).
[930](https://docs.rs#930)    let mut line_indent_ws: Option<&str> = None;
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    // The depth of the most recent *code* line, and whether the most recent content line was a
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    // comment. Used to detect the start of a block: a code statement deeper than the previous code
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    // line, with no comment in between, is a suite's first statement — gdformat strips a blank between
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    // a compound header and its body. A comment is the block's "first content" (its trailing blanks
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    // are kept), so an intervening comment suppresses the strip.
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    let mut prev_content_depth: usize = 0;
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    let mut prev_was_comment = false;
[938](https://docs.rs#938)
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    for (idx, t) in toks.iter().enumerate() {
[940](https://docs.rs#940)        let text = &source[t.range];
[941](https://docs.rs#941)        match t.kind {
[942](https://docs.rs#942)            SyntaxKind::Indent => depth += 1,
[943](https://docs.rs#943)            SyntaxKind::Dedent => depth = depth.saturating_sub(1),
[944](https://docs.rs#944)            // A synthetic line break: ends the logical line; the next one is re-indented. A synthetic
[945](https://docs.rs#945)            // `Newline` only follows a statement, so it always terminates a content line.
[946](https://docs.rs#946)            SyntaxKind::Newline => {
[947](https://docs.rs#947)                trim_trailing_inline_ws(&mut out);
[948](https://docs.rs#948)                if stack.is_empty() {
[949](https://docs.rs#949)                    // A normal logical-line break: the next line is re-indented from `depth`.
[950](https://docs.rs#950)                    emit_break(
[951](https://docs.rs#951)                        &mut out,
[952](https://docs.rs#952)                        collapse_on,
[953](https://docs.rs#953)                        &mut line_had_content,
[954](https://docs.rs#954)                        &mut pending_blanks,
[955](https://docs.rs#955)                    );
[956](https://docs.rs#956)                    line_start = true;
[957](https://docs.rs#957)                    prev_sig = None;
[958](https://docs.rs#958)                } else {
[959](https://docs.rs#959)                    // A synthetic break *inside brackets* is a multi-line lambda-body line break:
[960](https://docs.rs#960)                    // the prepass suppresses synthetic layout inside brackets EXCEPT for a lambda
[961](https://docs.rs#961)                    // body, for which it re-emits `Newline`/`Indent`/`Dedent`. Treat it like a
[962](https://docs.rs#962)                    // `NewlinePhys` continuation and keep the bracketed interior verbatim — do NOT
[963](https://docs.rs#963)                    // re-indent the body from `depth`. The body's verbatim-aligned *header* arrives
[964](https://docs.rs#964)                    // via `NewlinePhys` (kept verbatim), so depth-re-indenting only the body makes
[965](https://docs.rs#965)                    // the two disagree and produces non-parsing output. Canonical reflow of a
[966](https://docs.rs#966)                    // bracketed lambda block is the increment-C reflow's job, not the indenter's.
[967](https://docs.rs#967)                    out.push('\n');
[968](https://docs.rs#968)                    cont_line_start = true;
[969](https://docs.rs#969)                }
[970](https://docs.rs#970)                just_broke = true;
[971](https://docs.rs#971)                node_path = false;
[972](https://docs.rs#972)                pending_ws = None;
[973](https://docs.rs#973)                line_indent_ws = None;
[974](https://docs.rs#974)                pending_enum = false; // an `enum` keyword is consumed by its `{` within one line
[975](https://docs.rs#975)            }
[976](https://docs.rs#976)            SyntaxKind::NewlinePhys => {
[977](https://docs.rs#977)                if just_broke {
[978](https://docs.rs#978)                    just_broke = false; // its bytes belong to the synthetic break already emitted
[979](https://docs.rs#979)                } else {
[980](https://docs.rs#980)                    trim_trailing_inline_ws(&mut out);
[981](https://docs.rs#981)                    node_path = false;
[982](https://docs.rs#982)                    pending_ws = None;
[983](https://docs.rs#983)                    // Outside brackets this ends a comment-only line (content) or a blank line, and
[984](https://docs.rs#984)                    // the next line is re-indented. Inside brackets it is a real continuation — keep
[985](https://docs.rs#985)                    // the next line's alignment verbatim and never collapse it.
[986](https://docs.rs#986)                    if stack.is_empty() {
[987](https://docs.rs#987)                        emit_break(
[988](https://docs.rs#988)                            &mut out,
[989](https://docs.rs#989)                            collapse_on,
[990](https://docs.rs#990)                            &mut line_had_content,
[991](https://docs.rs#991)                            &mut pending_blanks,
[992](https://docs.rs#992)                        );
[993](https://docs.rs#993)                        line_start = true;
[994](https://docs.rs#994)                        prev_sig = None;
[995](https://docs.rs#995)                        line_indent_ws = None;
[996](https://docs.rs#996)                    } else {
[997](https://docs.rs#997)                        out.push('\n');
[998](https://docs.rs#998)                        cont_line_start = true;
[999](https://docs.rs#999)                    }
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)                }
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)            }
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)            SyntaxKind::Whitespace => {
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)                if line_start {
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)                    // Leading indentation — dropped; re-synthesized at the first significant token.
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)                    // Remember it: a *comment*'s authored indentation is recovered from it below.
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)                    line_indent_ws = Some(text);
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)                } else if spacing_on {
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)                    pending_ws = Some(text); // buffered; the next token decides whether to keep it.
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)                } else {
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)                    out.push_str(text); // indentation-only mode: original verbatim behavior.
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)                }
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)            }
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)            // A significant token or a comment.
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)            _ => {
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)                if line_start {
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)                    // A block-boundary *comment* is attributed by the prepass to the wrong raw
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)                    // `depth` (the `Indent`/`Dedent` lands on the next *code* line, not the comment).
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)                    // Recover its intended depth the way gdformat does: its authored indentation level
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)                    // clamped down to the deepest open block (`min(authored, max(prev, next))`).
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)                    let is_comment = matches!(
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)                        t.kind,
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)                        SyntaxKind::LineComment
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)                            | SyntaxKind::DocComment
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)                            | SyntaxKind::RegionComment
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)                            | SyntaxKind::EndRegionComment
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)                    );
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)                    let comment_len = line_indent_ws.map_or(0, str::len);
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)                    let emit_depth = if is_comment {
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)                        if comment_len == 0 {
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)                            // gdformat keeps a column-0 comment (`line.startswith("#")`) at column 0 —
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)                            // e.g. file-spanning `#region`/`#endregion` markers — rather than indenting
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)                            // it to the enclosing block.
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)                            0
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)                        } else {
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)                            let (next_depth, _) = next_code_info(&toks, idx, depth);
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)                            let unit_len = unit.len().max(1);
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)                            comment_depth(comment_len / unit_len, depth, next_depth)
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)                        }
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)                    } else {
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)                        depth
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)                    };
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)                    // Flush the buffered blank lines. gdformat squeezes *every* run of blank lines to a
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)                    // single blank, then re-inserts the 2nd (top-level) / 1st (nested) blank only around
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)                    // definitions (done later by `insert_def_blanks`). So the cap here is 1 everywhere,
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)                    // 0 before the first content (leading blanks gone), and 0 at the **start of a block**
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)                    // (a suite's first statement directly under its header — gdformat's
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)                    // `_remove_empty_strings_from_begin` strips a blank between a header and its body).
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)                    // The strip fires only for a *code* statement deeper than the previous code line
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)                    // with **no comment in between**: a comment is the block's first content, so its
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)                    // trailing blanks are kept (and a column-0 comment, whose raw `depth` lags, never
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)                    // looks like a header). This mirrors gdformat's `previous_statement_name is None`.
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)                    if collapse_on {
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)                        let at_block_start =
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)                            !prev_was_comment && !is_comment && depth > prev_content_depth;
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)                        let cap = if at_block_start {
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)                            0
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)                        } else {
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)                            usize::from(seen_content)
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)                        };
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)                        for _ in 0..pending_blanks.min(cap) {
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)                            out.push('\n');
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)                        }
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)                        pending_blanks = 0;
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)                    }
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)                    prev_was_comment = is_comment;
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)                    if !is_comment {
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)                        prev_content_depth = depth;
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)                    }
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)                    for _ in 0..emit_depth {
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)                        out.push_str(&unit);
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)                    }
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)                    line_start = false;
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)                    cont_line_start = false;
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)                } else if spacing_on {
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)                    if cont_line_start {
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)                        // First token of a bracketed continuation: keep its leading alignment.
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)                        if let Some(ws) = pending_ws {
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)                            out.push_str(ws);
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)                        }
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)                        cont_line_start = false;
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)                    } else if matches!(
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)                        t.kind,
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)                        SyntaxKind::LineComment
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)                            | SyntaxKind::DocComment
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)                            | SyntaxKind::RegionComment
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)                            | SyntaxKind::EndRegionComment
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)                    ) {
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)                        // An inline (trailing) comment is offset by exactly two spaces (gdformat's
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)                        // `INLINE_COMMENT_OFFSET`), regardless of the original spacing.
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)                        out.push_str("  ");
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)                        node_path = false;
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)                    } else if t.kind.is_trivia() {
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)                        // A line-continuation / BOM: keep the original spacing before it.
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)                        if let Some(ws) = pending_ws {
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)                            out.push_str(ws);
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)                        }
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)                        node_path = false;
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)                    } else {
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)                        // A significant token: synthesize the spacing. Inside a node-path run we
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)                        // keep the *original* spacing verbatim — a real `$Node/Path` is already
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)                        // tight (so it stays tight), and we must never *collapse* a genuinely-spaced
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)                        // `$A / b` (a division) into a node path, which would silently change meaning
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)                        // with an identical token sequence (the safety net cannot catch it).
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)                        let path_continue = node_path
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)                            && (matches!(
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)                                t.kind,
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)                                SyntaxKind::Ident | SyntaxKind::Slash | SyntaxKind::String
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)                            ) || (t.kind == SyntaxKind::Percent
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)                                && matches!(
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)                                    prev_sig,
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)                                    Some(SyntaxKind::Dollar | SyntaxKind::Slash)
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)                                )));
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)                        let spacing = if path_continue {
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)                            // A `%` in sigil position (`$%Unique`, `$A/%Unique`) continues the path; a
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)                            // `%` after an identifier is modulo and falls through to `space_before`.
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)                            Spacing::Verbatim
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)                        } else {
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)                            node_path = false; // any non-path token ends the run.
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)                            match prev_sig {
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)                                Some(p) => {
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)                                    let top_enum = stack.last() == Some(&SyntaxKind::LBrace)
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)                                        && brace_is_enum.last() == Some(&true);
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)                                    space_before(
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)                                        p,
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)                                        t.kind,
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)                                        stack.last().copied(),
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)                                        prev_unary,
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)                                        top_enum,
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)                                    )
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)                                }
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)                                None => Spacing::None,
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)                            }
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)                        };
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)                        match spacing {
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)                            Spacing::None => {}
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)                            Spacing::Single => out.push(' '),
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)                            Spacing::Verbatim => {
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)                                if let Some(ws) = pending_ws {
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)                                    out.push_str(ws);
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)                                }
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)                            }
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)                        }
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)                    }
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)                }
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)                pending_ws = None;
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)                just_broke = false;
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)                // String literals are normalized to gdformat's canonical quote style (value-
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)                // preserving; guarded by the meaning-equivalence net). Everything else is verbatim.
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)                if config.normalize_strings
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)                    && matches!(
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)                        t.kind,
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)                        SyntaxKind::String | SyntaxKind::StringName | SyntaxKind::NodePath
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)                    )
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)                {
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)                    out.push_str(&canonical_string(text));
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)                } else {
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)                    out.push_str(text);
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)                }
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)                // Any token reaching here (a significant token or a comment) is line content.
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)                line_had_content = true;
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)                seen_content = true;
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)                match t.kind {
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)                    SyntaxKind::LBrace => {
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)                        stack.push(t.kind);
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)                        brace_is_enum.push(pending_enum);
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)                        pending_enum = false;
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)                    }
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)                    SyntaxKind::LParen | SyntaxKind::LBrack => {
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)                        stack.push(t.kind);
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)                    }
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)                    SyntaxKind::RBrace => {
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)                        stack.pop();
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)                        brace_is_enum.pop();
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)                    }
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)                    SyntaxKind::RParen | SyntaxKind::RBrack => {
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)                        stack.pop();
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)                    }
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)                    _ => {}
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)                }
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)                // Spacing state — significant tokens only (a comment is never an operand).
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)                if !t.kind.is_trivia() {
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)                    if t.kind == SyntaxKind::EnumKw {
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)                        pending_enum = true; // the next `{` opens an enum body
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)                    }
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)                    let unary_ctx = prev_sig.is_none_or(|p| !is_operand_end(p));
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)                    // Enter node-path mode after a `$` (always) or a `%` in sigil position (a `%`
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)                    // after an operand is modulo, and stays a normal binary operator).
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)                    if t.kind == SyntaxKind::Dollar || (t.kind == SyntaxKind::Percent && unary_ctx)
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)                    {
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)                        node_path = true;
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)                    }
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)                    prev_unary = match t.kind {
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)                        SyntaxKind::Minus | SyntaxKind::Plus => unary_ctx,
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)                        SyntaxKind::Tilde | SyntaxKind::Bang => true,
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)                        _ => false,
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)                    };
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)                    // A soft keyword (`match`/`when`) used as a *member* (`obj.match`) is an ordinary
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)                    // identifier operand — record it as `Ident` so a following `(` hugs it
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)                    // (`obj.match(x)`), while a leading `match (x):` statement keeps its space.
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)                    let member_soft_kw = matches!(t.kind, SyntaxKind::MatchKw | SyntaxKind::WhenKw)
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)                        && prev_sig == Some(SyntaxKind::Dot);
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)                    prev_sig = Some(if member_soft_kw {
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)                        SyntaxKind::Ident
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)                    } else {
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)                        t.kind
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)                    });
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)                }
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)            }
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)        }
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)    }
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)    // Trim a trailing blank/whitespace run and guarantee exactly one final newline.
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)    let trimmed = out.trim_end();
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)    let mut result = String::with_capacity(trimmed.len() + 1);
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)    result.push_str(trimmed);
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)    if !result.is_empty() {
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)        result.push('\n');
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)    }
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)    result
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)}
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)/// The role a statement (logical) line plays in the blank-line-insertion policy.
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)enum LineRole {
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)    /// A `func` / `static func` / `class` declaration — gdformat surrounds these with blank lines.
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)    Def,
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)    /// A standalone comment line (`#` / `##`) — attaches to a following statement.
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)    Comment,
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)    /// A standalone annotation line (`@foo` with nothing else on the line) — attaches to a following
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)    /// statement.
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)    Annotation,
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)    /// Any other statement (`var` / `const` / `signal` / `class_name` / an expression / …).
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)    Other,
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)}
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)/// A statement-level "head" line discovered in already-formatted text: its 0-based physical line
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)/// number, its block depth, and its [`LineRole`]. Bracket-continuation and lambda-body lines are
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)/// not heads.
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)struct HeadLine {
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)    line: usize,
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)    depth: usize,
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)    role: LineRole,
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)}
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)/// One logical unit for the blank-line edge rule: a definition (or other statement) together with
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)/// any comment/annotation prefix that attaches to it. `head_line` is the unit's first physical line.
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)struct Unit {
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)    head_line: usize,
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)    depth: usize,
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)    is_def: bool,
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)    /// A *standalone* comment (not a prefix that attaches to a following def/statement). gdformat does
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)    /// not force blank lines around such a comment (e.g. a trailing `#endregion`), and it is
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)    /// transparent to the surrounding defs' blank-line spacing.
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)    is_comment: bool,
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)    /// The unit is a definition reached through an **annotation** prefix (`@rpc func …`). gdformat
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)    /// forces blanks before such a unit only when the *previous* sibling was itself a def — not on the
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)    /// unit's own def-ness (the annotation line, not the def, owns the leading blanks, and an
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)    /// annotation is absent from the surrounding-empty-lines table). A *comment*-prefixed def forces
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)    /// like a plain def.
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)    ann_prefixed: bool,
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)}
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)/// Classify the statement line whose first significant-or-comment token is `toks[start]`. Scans the
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)/// rest of the logical line (across bracketed continuations) to look past an annotation prefix.
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)fn classify_line(toks: &[gdscript_syntax::RawToken], start: usize) -> LineRole {
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)    if matches!(
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)        toks[start].kind,
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)        S::LineComment | S::DocComment | S::RegionComment | S::EndRegionComment
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    ) {
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)        return LineRole::Comment;
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)    }
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)    // Collect the line's significant token kinds (skip trivia; stop at the logical line end).
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)    let mut kinds: Vec<S> = Vec::new();
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)    let mut local_stack = 0usize;
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)    for t in &toks[start..] {
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)        match t.kind {
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)            S::Newline => break,
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)            S::NewlinePhys if local_stack == 0 => break,
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)            S::LParen | S::LBrack | S::LBrace => {
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)                local_stack += 1;
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)                kinds.push(t.kind);
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)            }
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)            S::RParen | S::RBrack | S::RBrace => {
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)                local_stack = local_stack.saturating_sub(1);
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)                kinds.push(t.kind);
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)            }
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)            k if k.is_trivia() || k.is_synthetic_layout() => {}
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)            k => kinds.push(k),
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)        }
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)    }
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)    // Skip a leading annotation prefix: `@ Ident (balanced parens)?`, repeated.
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)    let mut i = 0;
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)    while kinds.get(i) == Some(&S::At) {
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)        i += 1; // `@`
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)        if kinds.get(i) == Some(&S::Ident) {
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)            i += 1; // annotation name
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)        }
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)        if kinds.get(i) == Some(&S::LParen) {
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)            // skip the balanced argument list
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)            let mut d = 0usize;
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)            while let Some(&k) = kinds.get(i) {
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)                i += 1;
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)                match k {
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)                    S::LParen => d += 1,
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)                    S::RParen => {
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)                        d -= 1;
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)                        if d == 0 {
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)                            break;
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)                        }
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)                    }
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)                    _ => {}
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)                }
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)            }
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)        }
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)    }
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)    match kinds.get(i) {
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)        None => LineRole::Annotation, // an annotation alone on its line
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)        Some(S::FuncKw | S::ClassKw) => LineRole::Def,
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)        Some(S::StaticKw) if kinds.get(i + 1) == Some(&S::FuncKw) => LineRole::Def,
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)        _ => LineRole::Other,
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)    }
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)}
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)/// Insert blank lines around definitions to match gdformat's policy (2 around top-level defs, 1
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)/// around nested defs), operating on already-formatted, already-collapsed text. Purely additive —
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)/// it only inserts blank lines, so it never changes the significant token sequence. Idempotent: the
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)/// blanks it would add are already present on a second pass.
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)#[allow(
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)    clippy::too_many_lines,
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)    reason = "three cohesive sequential passes (find heads, group units, apply the edge rule) over the same token stream; clearer kept together than split"
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333))]
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)fn insert_def_blanks(formatted: &str, config: &FmtConfig) -> String {
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)    let raw = gdscript_syntax::tokenize(formatted);
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)    let (toks, _diags) = gdscript_syntax::run_prepass(&raw, formatted);
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)    let lines: Vec<&str> = formatted.lines().collect();
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)    let is_blank: Vec<bool> = lines.iter().map(|l| l.trim().is_empty()).collect();
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)    let blank_above = |l: usize| l > 0 && is_blank.get(l - 1).copied().unwrap_or(false);
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)    // Byte offset -> 0-based physical line number. Built from the raw bytes (so newlines *inside*
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)    // multi-line string tokens count too) — `formatted.lines()` indices must align with this.
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)    let line_starts: Vec<usize> = std::iter::once(0)
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)        .chain(
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)            formatted
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)                .bytes()
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)                .enumerate()
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)                .filter_map(|(i, b)| (b == b'\n').then_some(i + 1)),
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)        )
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)        .collect();
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)    let line_of = |offset: usize| line_starts.partition_point(|&s| s <= offset) - 1;
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)    // The (already-normalized) leading-indentation depth of a formatted line.
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)    let line_depth = |l: usize| -> usize {
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)        let s = lines.get(l).copied().unwrap_or("");
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)        if config.use_tabs {
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)            s.bytes().take_while(|&b| b == b'\t').count()
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)        } else {
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)            s.bytes()
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)                .take_while(|&b| b == b' ')
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)                .count()
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)                .checked_div(config.indent_size)
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)                .unwrap_or(0)
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)        }
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)    };
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)    // --- pass 1: find statement-level head lines (skip bracket / lambda continuations) ---
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)    let mut heads: Vec<HeadLine> = Vec::new();
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)    let mut depth = 0usize;
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)    let mut stack = 0usize;
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)    let mut this_line_continues = false; // a trailing `\` continues onto the next physical line
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)    let mut next_line_is_cont = false; // the logical line we are about to start is a continuation
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)    let mut seen_first_on_line = false;
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)    for (idx, t) in toks.iter().enumerate() {
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)        match t.kind {
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)            S::Indent => depth += 1,
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)            S::Dedent => depth = depth.saturating_sub(1),
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)            S::NewlinePhys => {
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)                next_line_is_cont = stack > 0 || this_line_continues;
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)                this_line_continues = false;
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)                seen_first_on_line = false;
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)            }
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)            S::LineContinuation => this_line_continues = true,
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)            S::Newline | S::Whitespace | S::Bom => {}
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)            _ => {
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)                if !seen_first_on_line {
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)                    seen_first_on_line = true;
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)                    if stack == 0 && !next_line_is_cont {
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)                        let line = line_of(usize::from(t.range.start()));
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)                        let role = classify_line(&toks, idx);
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)                        // A comment's *structural* block (which one it belongs to, for the edge
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)                        // rule) is not its visual indentation: a comment whose *next* code is deeper
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)                        // than the comment's own column belongs to that deeper block — even a column-0
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)                        // comment sitting amid a function body (commented-out code) is inside the
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)                        // function, not a sibling of the preceding def. Otherwise it sits at its own
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)                        // (visual) depth, which correctly attaches a column-0 doc-comment to a
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)                        // following *dedented* def (whose next code is at column 0, not deeper).
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)                        let head_depth = if role == LineRole::Comment {
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)                            let visual = line_depth(line);
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)                            let next_depth = next_code_info(&toks, idx, depth).0;
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)                            if next_depth > visual {
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)                                next_depth
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)                            } else {
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)                                visual
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)                            }
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)                        } else {
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)                            depth
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)                        };
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)                        heads.push(HeadLine {
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)                            line,
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)                            depth: head_depth,
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)                            role,
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)                        });
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)                    }
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)                }
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)                match t.kind {
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)                    S::LParen | S::LBrack | S::LBrace => stack += 1,
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)                    S::RParen | S::RBrack | S::RBrace => stack = stack.saturating_sub(1),
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)                    _ => {}
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)                }
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)            }
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)        }
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)    }
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)    // --- pass 2: group heads into units (a def/statement + its attached comment/annotation prefix) ---
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)    let mut units: Vec<Unit> = Vec::new();
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)    let mut i = 0;
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)    while i < heads.len() {
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)        let h = heads[i];
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)        if matches!(h.role, LineRole::Comment | LineRole::Annotation) {
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)            // Accumulate a contiguous, same-depth prefix run of comments/annotations.
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)            let mut j = i + 1;
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)            while j < heads.len()
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)                && matches!(heads[j].role, LineRole::Comment | LineRole::Annotation)
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)                && heads[j].depth == h.depth
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)                && !blank_above(heads[j].line)
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)            {
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)                j += 1;
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)            }
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)            // Does a same-depth statement follow contiguously (no blank gap)? Then the run attaches.
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)            if j < heads.len()
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)                && heads[j].depth == h.depth
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)                && !blank_above(heads[j].line)
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)                && matches!(heads[j].role, LineRole::Def | LineRole::Other)
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)            {
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)                units.push(Unit {
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)                    head_line: h.line,
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)                    depth: h.depth,
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)                    is_def: heads[j].role == LineRole::Def,
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)                    is_comment: false,
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)                    ann_prefixed: h.role == LineRole::Annotation,
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)                });
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)                i = j + 1;
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)            } else {
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)                // Standalone comment/annotation lines (each its own non-def unit).
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)                for h in &heads[i..j] {
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)                    units.push(Unit {
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)                        head_line: h.line,
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)                        depth: h.depth,
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)                        is_def: false,
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)                        is_comment: h.role == LineRole::Comment,
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)                        ann_prefixed: false,
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)                    });
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)                }
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)                i = j;
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)            }
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)        } else {
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)            units.push(Unit {
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)                head_line: h.line,
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)                depth: h.depth,
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)                is_def: h.role == LineRole::Def,
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)                is_comment: false,
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)                ann_prefixed: false,
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)            });
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)            i += 1;
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)        }
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)    }
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)    // --- pass 3: the edge rule — N blanks before a unit whose own or previous sibling is a def ---
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)    let mut required: std::collections::HashMap<usize, usize> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)    let mut last_is_def: Vec<Option<bool>> = Vec::new();
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)    for (k, u) in units.iter().enumerate() {
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)        while last_is_def.len() <= u.depth {
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)            last_is_def.push(None);
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)        }
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)        let prev = last_is_def[u.depth];
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)        let first_in_block = prev.is_none();
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)        let n = if u.depth == 0 { 2 } else { 1 };
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)        // A *trailing* standalone comment — one that ends its block (no following unit at its depth or
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)        // shallower-after) such as a closing `#endregion` — keeps its source blanks unforced, matching
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)        // gdformat's end-of-block reconstruction. A standalone comment *between* statements still
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)        // resets def-adjacency (a following statement's spacing is measured from it, not the def above).
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)        let trailing_comment = u.is_comment && units.get(k + 1).is_none_or(|nx| nx.depth < u.depth);
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)        // An annotation-prefixed def forces blanks only after a previous def; a plain or
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)        // comment-prefixed def also forces on its own def-ness.
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)        let needs = if u.ann_prefixed {
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)            prev == Some(true)
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)        } else {
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)            u.is_def || prev == Some(true)
[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)        };
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)        if !trailing_comment && !first_in_block && needs {
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)            required.insert(u.head_line, n);
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)        }
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)        last_is_def[u.depth] = Some(u.is_def);
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)        last_is_def.truncate(u.depth + 1); // entering a deeper block starts its siblings fresh
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)    }
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)    if required.is_empty() {
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)        return formatted.to_owned();
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)    }
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)    // --- rebuild: top up the blank run before each required head to exactly N ---
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)    let mut out = String::with_capacity(formatted.len() + required.len() * 2);
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)    let mut trailing_blanks = 0usize;
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)    for (lno, content) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)        if let Some(&k) = required.get(&lno) {
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)            for _ in trailing_blanks..k {
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)                out.push('\n');
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)            }
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)        }
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)        out.push_str(content);
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)        out.push('\n');
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)        trailing_blanks = if is_blank[lno] {
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)            trailing_blanks + 1
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)        } else {
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)            0
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)        };
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)    }
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)    out
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)}
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)// ===================== line reflow (length-driven wrapping) =====================
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)//
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)// A statement that does not fit in `line_width` and contains a bracketed group is wrapped the way
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)// gdformat does: try the group **flat**; if it does not fit, **compact** (all elements on one
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)// indented continuation line, close bracket on its own line); if even that does not fit, **exploded**
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)// (one element per line, recursively). A **magic trailing comma** in the source forces a group
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)// exploded-with-comma even when it would fit (and forces every enclosing group multi-line) — the one
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)// case that mutates the token sequence (a trailing comma), guarded by the meaning-equivalence net.
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)// Only statements that occupy a single physical line are reflowed (so the pass is trivially
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)// idempotent — a wrapped statement spans bracket-continuation lines that are skipped on the next run).
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)/// One rendered token: its kind, text, and whether a single space precedes it in the flat form.
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)struct Atom {
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)    kind: SyntaxKind,
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)    text: String,
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)    space: bool,
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)}
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)/// A reflow document node: a text run, or a bracketed group of comma-separated element sequences.
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)enum ReflowDoc {
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)    Text {
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)        text: String,
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)        space: bool,
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)    },
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)    Group {
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)        space: bool,
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)        open: String,
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)        elems: Vec<Vec<ReflowDoc>>,
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)        close: &'static str,
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)        /// The source had a **magic trailing comma** — gdformat forces this group exploded one per
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)        /// line *with* the trailing comma, even when it would fit.
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)        magic: bool,
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)    },
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)}
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)/// Whether a group must be broken across lines: it has a magic trailing comma, or a descendant does
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)/// (a magic comma anywhere forces every enclosing group multi-line, matching gdformat).
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)fn group_forced(elems: &[Vec<ReflowDoc>], magic: bool) -> bool {
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)    magic
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)        || elems.iter().any(|e| {
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)            e.iter().any(|d| match d {
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)                ReflowDoc::Group { elems, magic, .. } => group_forced(elems, *magic),
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)                ReflowDoc::Text { .. } => false,
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)            })
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)        })
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)}
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)fn open_close(text: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)    match text {
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)        "(" => Some(")"),
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)        "[" => Some("]"),
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)        "{" => Some("}"),
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)        _ => None,
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)    }
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)}
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)/// Display columns of a content string (no tabs — those only appear in leading indentation).
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)fn cols(s: &str) -> usize {
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)    s.chars().count()
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)}
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)/// Display width of a full line, counting a leading tab as `tw` columns.
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)fn display_cols(line: &str, tw: usize) -> usize {
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)    line.chars().map(|c| if c == '\t' { tw } else { 1 }).sum()
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)}
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)/// Build the comma-separated element sequences of a group whose contents start at `atoms[*i]`,
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)/// consuming through the matching `close` (or to the end when `close` is `None`, for the top level).
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)/// Returns the elements and whether the group ended with a magic trailing comma.
[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)fn build_elems(atoms: &[Atom], i: &mut usize, close: Option<&str>) -> (Vec<Vec<ReflowDoc>>, bool) {
[1602](https://docs.rs#1602)    let mut elems: Vec<Vec<ReflowDoc>> = Vec::new();
[1603](https://docs.rs#1603)    let mut cur: Vec<ReflowDoc> = Vec::new();
[1604](https://docs.rs#1604)    let mut elem_start = true;
[1605](https://docs.rs#1605)    while *i < atoms.len() {
[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)        let a = &atoms[*i];
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)        if close == Some(a.text.as_str()) {
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)            *i += 1;
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)            break;
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)        }
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)        if a.text == "," {
[1612](https://docs.rs#1612)            elems.push(std::mem::take(&mut cur));
[1613](https://docs.rs#1613)            elem_start = true;
[1614](https://docs.rs#1614)            *i += 1;
[1615](https://docs.rs#1615)            continue;
[1616](https://docs.rs#1616)        }
[1617](https://docs.rs#1617)        let space = !elem_start && a.space;
[1618](https://docs.rs#1618)        if let Some(cl) = open_close(&a.text) {
[1619](https://docs.rs#1619)            let open = a.text.clone();
[1620](https://docs.rs#1620)            *i += 1;
[1621](https://docs.rs#1621)            let (inner, magic) = build_elems(atoms, i, Some(cl));
[1622](https://docs.rs#1622)            cur.push(ReflowDoc::Group {
[1623](https://docs.rs#1623)                space,
[1624](https://docs.rs#1624)                open,
[1625](https://docs.rs#1625)                elems: inner,
[1626](https://docs.rs#1626)                close: cl,
[1627](https://docs.rs#1627)                magic,
[1628](https://docs.rs#1628)            });
[1629](https://docs.rs#1629)        } else {
[1630](https://docs.rs#1630)            cur.push(ReflowDoc::Text {
[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)                text: a.text.clone(),
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)                space,
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)            });
[1634](https://docs.rs#1634)            *i += 1;
[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)        }
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)        elem_start = false;
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)    }
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)    // A trailing comma leaves `elem_start` set with `cur` empty after at least one real element.
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)    let magic = elem_start && !elems.is_empty();
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)    if !cur.is_empty() {
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)        elems.push(cur);
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)    }
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)    (elems, magic)
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)}
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)fn flat_seq(docs: &[ReflowDoc]) -> String {
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)    let mut out = String::new();
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)    for d in docs {
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)        match d {
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)            ReflowDoc::Text { text, space } => {
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)                if *space {
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)                    out.push(' ');
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)                }
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)                out.push_str(text);
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)            }
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)            ReflowDoc::Group {
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)                space,
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)                open,
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)                elems,
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)                close,
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)                magic,
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)            } => {
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)                if *space {
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)                    out.push(' ');
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)                }
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)                out.push_str(open);
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)                out.push_str(&flat_group_contents(elems, *magic));
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)                out.push_str(close);
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)            }
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)        }
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)    }
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)    out
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)}
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)fn flat_group_contents(elems: &[Vec<ReflowDoc>], magic: bool) -> String {
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)    let mut s = elems
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)        .iter()
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)        .map(|e| flat_seq(e))
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)        .join(", ");
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)    if magic && !elems.is_empty() {
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)        s.push(',');
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)    }
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)    s
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)}
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)/// Render a sequence (one element) at base `indent`, starting at column `col`, wrapping any group
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)/// that does not fit. Returns the text and the ending column.
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)fn render_seq(
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)    docs: &[ReflowDoc],
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)    indent: usize,
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)    mut col: usize,
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)    cfg: &FmtConfig,
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)    tw: usize,
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)    unit: &str,
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)) -> (String, usize) {
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)    let mut out = String::new();
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)    // Flat width of each doc, so a group knows the width of the content that *follows* it on the line
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)    // (its "tail") — a group must wrap when the group + its tail overflow, even if the group alone fits.
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)    let widths: Vec<usize> = docs
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)        .iter()
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)        .map(|d| cols(&flat_seq(std::slice::from_ref(d))))
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)        .collect();
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)    let total: usize = widths.iter().sum();
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)    // gdformat wraps the *outermost* (last) bracket group — except a `func`/`static func` definition,
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)    // whose **parameter list** (the first group) is the one that wraps, not a `-> Array[T]` return
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)    // type. An earlier group otherwise stays flat unless it is itself forced (a magic comma).
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)    let first_text = match docs.first() {
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)        Some(ReflowDoc::Text { text, .. }) => Some(text.as_str()),
[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)        _ => None,
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)    };
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)    let is_def = first_text == Some("func")
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)        || (first_text == Some("static")
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)            && matches!(docs.get(1), Some(ReflowDoc::Text { text, .. }) if text == "func"));
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)    let wrap_target = if is_def {
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)        docs.iter()
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)            .position(|d| matches!(d, ReflowDoc::Group { .. }))
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)    } else {
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)        docs.iter()
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)            .rposition(|d| matches!(d, ReflowDoc::Group { .. }))
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)    };
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)    let mut before = 0usize;
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)    for (i, d) in docs.iter().enumerate() {
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)        let tail = total - before - widths[i];
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)        match d {
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)            ReflowDoc::Text { text, space } => {
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)                if *space {
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)                    out.push(' ');
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)                    col += 1;
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)                }
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)                out.push_str(text);
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)                col += cols(text);
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)            }
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)            ReflowDoc::Group {
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)                space,
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)                open,
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)                elems,
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)                close,
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)                magic,
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)            } => {
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)                if *space {
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)                    out.push(' ');
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)                    col += 1;
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)                }
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)                let (g, end) = if Some(i) == wrap_target || group_forced(elems, *magic) {
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)                    render_group(open, elems, close, *magic, indent, col, tail, cfg, tw, unit)
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)                } else {
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)                    let flat = format!("{open}{}{close}", flat_group_contents(elems, *magic));
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)                    let end = col + cols(&flat);
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)                    (flat, end)
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)                };
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)                out.push_str(&g);
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)                col = end;
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)            }
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)        }
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)        before += widths[i];
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)    }
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)    (out, col)
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)}
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)#[allow(
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)    clippy::too_many_arguments,
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)    reason = "a focused internal renderer threading layout state"
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764))]
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)fn render_group(
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)    open: &str,
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)    elems: &[Vec<ReflowDoc>],
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)    close: &str,
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)    magic: bool,
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)    indent: usize,
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)    col: usize,
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)    tail: usize,
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)    cfg: &FmtConfig,
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)    tw: usize,
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)    unit: &str,
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)) -> (String, usize) {
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)    let forced = group_forced(elems, magic);
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)    // flat: the whole group on the current line (only when it — plus the content that follows it on
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)    // the line — fits, and it is not forced multi-line).
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)    let flat = format!("{open}{}{close}", flat_group_contents(elems, magic));
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)    if !forced && (col + cols(&flat) + tail <= cfg.line_width || elems.is_empty()) {
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)        let end = col + cols(&flat);
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)        return (flat, end);
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)    }
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)    let inner = indent + 1;
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)    let inner_col = inner * tw;
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)    let close_end = indent * tw + cols(close);
