[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)    // compact: all elements on one indented continuation line (not when forced exploded).
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)    if !forced {
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)        let contents = flat_group_contents(elems, magic);
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)        if inner_col + cols(&contents) <= cfg.line_width {
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)            let s = format!(
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)                "{open}\n{ind}{contents}\n{base}{close}",
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)                ind = unit.repeat(inner),
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)                base = unit.repeat(indent),
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)            );
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)            return (s, close_end);
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)        }
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)    }
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)    // exploded: one element per line (each rendered recursively). A comma follows every element
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)    // except the last — unless this group is magic, when it follows the last one too.
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)    let mut s = String::from(open);
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)    s.push('\n');
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)    for (k, elem) in elems.iter().enumerate() {
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)        s.push_str(&unit.repeat(inner));
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)        let (es, _) = render_seq(elem, inner, inner_col, cfg, tw, unit);
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)        s.push_str(&es);
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)        if magic || k + 1 < elems.len() {
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)            s.push(',');
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)        }
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)        s.push('\n');
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)    }
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)    s.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent));
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)    s.push_str(close);
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)    (s, close_end)
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)}

[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)/// Parse a single physical line's content into reflow atoms, or `None` if it is not a clean,
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)/// reflowable single-line statement (has a comment, an error/continuation token, or unbalanced /
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)/// negative bracket nesting). A magic trailing comma is kept (it drives gdformat's exploded mode).
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)fn line_atoms(body: &str) -> Option<Vec<Atom>> {
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)    let toks = gdscript_syntax::tokenize(body);
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)    let mut atoms: Vec<Atom> = Vec::new();
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)    let mut space = false;
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)    let mut depth: i32 = 0;
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)    for t in &toks {
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)        match t.kind {
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)            S::Whitespace => space = true,
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)            S::Bom => {}
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)            S::LineComment
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)            | S::DocComment
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)            | S::RegionComment
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)            | S::EndRegionComment
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)            | S::LineContinuation => return None,
[1836](https://docs.rs#1836)            k => {
[1837](https://docs.rs#1837)                if matches!(k, S::LParen | S::LBrack | S::LBrace) {
[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)                    depth += 1;
[1839](https://docs.rs#1839)                } else if matches!(k, S::RParen | S::RBrack | S::RBrace) {
[1840](https://docs.rs#1840)                    depth -= 1;
[1841](https://docs.rs#1841)                    if depth < 0 {
[1842](https://docs.rs#1842)                        return None;
[1843](https://docs.rs#1843)                    }
[1844](https://docs.rs#1844)                }
[1845](https://docs.rs#1845)                atoms.push(Atom {
[1846](https://docs.rs#1846)                    kind: k,
[1847](https://docs.rs#1847)                    text: body[t.range].to_string(),
[1848](https://docs.rs#1848)                    space,
[1849](https://docs.rs#1849)                });
[1850](https://docs.rs#1850)                space = false;
[1851](https://docs.rs#1851)            }
[1852](https://docs.rs#1852)        }
[1853](https://docs.rs#1853)    }
[1854](https://docs.rs#1854)    if depth != 0 {
[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)        return None;
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)    }
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)    Some(atoms)
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)}
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)/// Binary-operator precedence (lower binds looser → breaks first); `None` for non-binary tokens.
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)/// Mirrors the parser's `infix_prec`.
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)pub(crate) fn infix_prec(kind: SyntaxKind) -> Option<u8> {
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)    Some(match kind {
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)        S::OrKw | S::PipePipe => 4,
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)        S::AndKw | S::AmpAmp => 5,
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)        S::InKw => 7,
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)        S::EqEq | S::Neq | S::Lt | S::Gt | S::Le | S::Ge => 8,
[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)        S::Pipe => 9,
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)        S::Caret => 10,
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)        S::Amp => 11,
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)        S::Shl | S::Shr => 12,
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)        S::Plus | S::Minus => 13,
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)        S::Star | S::Slash | S::Percent => 14,
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)        S::StarStar => 17,
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)        _ => return None,
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)    })
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)}

[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)fn is_assign_op(kind: SyntaxKind) -> bool {
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)    matches!(
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)        kind,
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)        S::Eq
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)            | S::PlusEq
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)            | S::MinusEq
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)            | S::StarEq
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)            | S::SlashEq
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)            | S::StarStarEq
[1890](https://docs.rs#1890)            | S::PercentEq
[1891](https://docs.rs#1891)            | S::AmpEq
[1892](https://docs.rs#1892)            | S::PipeEq
[1893](https://docs.rs#1893)            | S::CaretEq
[1894](https://docs.rs#1894)            | S::ShlEq
[1895](https://docs.rs#1895)            | S::ShrEq
[1896](https://docs.rs#1896)            | S::ColonEq
[1897](https://docs.rs#1897)    )

[1900](https://docs.rs#1900)/// Flat-render a run of atoms (the first atom never gets a leading space).
[1901](https://docs.rs#1901)fn flat_atoms(atoms: &[Atom]) -> String {
[1902](https://docs.rs#1902)    let mut s = String::new();
[1903](https://docs.rs#1903)    for (i, a) in atoms.iter().enumerate() {
[1904](https://docs.rs#1904)        if i > 0 && a.space {
[1905](https://docs.rs#1905)            s.push(' ');
[1906](https://docs.rs#1906)        }
[1907](https://docs.rs#1907)        s.push_str(&a.text);
[1908](https://docs.rs#1908)    }
[1909](https://docs.rs#1909)    s
[1910](https://docs.rs#1910)}
[1911](https://docs.rs#1911)
[1912](https://docs.rs#1912)/// The `[prefix_end, suffix_start)` boundaries of the wrappable expression inside a statement's
[1913](https://docs.rs#1913)/// atoms: the condition of `if`/`elif`/`while` (excluding the trailing `:`), the value of `return`,
[1914](https://docs.rs#1914)/// or the right-hand side of a top-level assignment. `None` if there is no such expression.
[1915](https://docs.rs#1915)fn expression_span(atoms: &[Atom]) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
[1916](https://docs.rs#1916)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[1917](https://docs.rs#1917)    let first = atoms.first()?;
[1918](https://docs.rs#1918)    match first.kind {
[1919](https://docs.rs#1919)        S::IfKw | S::ElifKw | S::WhileKw => {
[1920](https://docs.rs#1920)            let suffix = if atoms.last()?.kind == S::Colon {
[1921](https://docs.rs#1921)                atoms.len() - 1
[1922](https://docs.rs#1922)            } else {
[1923](https://docs.rs#1923)                return None;
[1924](https://docs.rs#1924)            };
[1925](https://docs.rs#1925)            Some((1, suffix))
[1926](https://docs.rs#1926)        }
[1927](https://docs.rs#1927)        S::ReturnKw => Some((1, atoms.len())),
[1928](https://docs.rs#1928)        _ => {
[1929](https://docs.rs#1929)            let mut depth = 0i32;
[1930](https://docs.rs#1930)            for (i, a) in atoms.iter().enumerate() {
[1931](https://docs.rs#1931)                match a.kind {
[1932](https://docs.rs#1932)                    S::LParen | S::LBrack | S::LBrace => depth += 1,
[1933](https://docs.rs#1933)                    S::RParen | S::RBrack | S::RBrace => depth -= 1,
[1934](https://docs.rs#1934)                    k if depth == 0 && is_assign_op(k) => return Some((i + 1, atoms.len())),
[1935](https://docs.rs#1935)                    _ => {}
[1936](https://docs.rs#1936)                }
[1937](https://docs.rs#1937)            }
[1938](https://docs.rs#1938)            None
[1939](https://docs.rs#1939)        }
[1940](https://docs.rs#1940)    }
[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)}
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)/// Strip a redundant grouping paren that wraps the *entire* expression (e.g. the `(...)` this very
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)/// pass injected on a previous run) so re-flowing is idempotent. `(a and b)` → `a and b`, but
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)/// `(a + b) * c` is left alone (the paren is not the whole expression).
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)fn strip_redundant_parens(mut expr: &[Atom]) -> &[Atom] {
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)    while expr.len() >= 2 && expr[0].text == "(" {
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)        let mut depth = 0i32;
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)        let mut close = None;
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)        for (i, a) in expr.iter().enumerate() {
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)            if open_close(&a.text).is_some() {
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)                depth += 1;
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)            } else if matches!(a.text.as_str(), ")" | "]" | "}") {
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)                depth -= 1;
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)                if depth == 0 {
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)                    close = Some(i);
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)                    break;
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)                }
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)            }
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)        }
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)        if close == Some(expr.len() - 1) {
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)            expr = &expr[1..expr.len() - 1];
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)        } else {
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)            break;
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)        }
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)    }
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)    expr
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)}
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)/// The indices (within `expr`) of top-level **binary** operators, paired with their precedence. A
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)/// `+`/`-` etc. is binary only when it follows an operand (not at a unary position); and a `/`/`%`
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)/// inside a **node-path run** (`$Node/Path`, `%Unique/Child`) is a path separator, not an operator —
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)/// the parser reads `$A / B` as the same node-path as `$A/B`, so such a chain must never be split.
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)fn top_level_binary_ops(expr: &[Atom]) -> Vec<(usize, u8)> {
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)    let mut out = Vec::new();
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)    let mut depth = 0i32;
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)    let mut node_path = false;
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)    let mut prev_operand_end = false;
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)    for (i, a) in expr.iter().enumerate() {
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)        match a.kind {
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)            S::LParen | S::LBrack | S::LBrace => depth += 1,
[1983](https://docs.rs#1983)            S::RParen | S::RBrack | S::RBrace => depth -= 1,
[1984](https://docs.rs#1984)            _ => {}
[1985](https://docs.rs#1985)        }
[1986](https://docs.rs#1986)        let in_path = node_path && matches!(a.kind, S::Ident | S::Slash | S::String);
[1987](https://docs.rs#1987)        let binary_here = depth == 0 && !in_path && i > 0 && prev_operand_end;
[1988](https://docs.rs#1988)        if let Some(p) = infix_prec(a.kind).filter(|_| binary_here) {
[1989](https://docs.rs#1989)            out.push((i, p));
[1990](https://docs.rs#1990)        }
[1991](https://docs.rs#1991)        if node_path && !matches!(a.kind, S::Ident | S::Slash | S::String) {
[1992](https://docs.rs#1992)            node_path = false;
[1993](https://docs.rs#1993)        }
[1994](https://docs.rs#1994)        if a.kind == S::Dollar || (a.kind == S::Percent && !prev_operand_end) {
[1995](https://docs.rs#1995)            node_path = true;
[1996](https://docs.rs#1996)        }
[1997](https://docs.rs#1997)        prev_operand_end = is_operand_end(a.kind);
[1998](https://docs.rs#1998)    }
[1999](https://docs.rs#1999)    out
[2000](https://docs.rs#2000)}
[2001](https://docs.rs#2001)
[2002](https://docs.rs#2002)/// Wrap a too-long statement whose wrappable expression is a top-level **binary-operator chain** the
[2003](https://docs.rs#2003)/// way gdformat does: inject parens and break at the lowest-precedence top-level operator,
[2004](https://docs.rs#2004)/// operator-leading (each operand rendered recursively, so its own brackets reflow). `None` when
[2005](https://docs.rs#2005)/// there is no wrappable binary-operator expression.
[2006](https://docs.rs#2006)fn operator_chain_wrap(
[2007](https://docs.rs#2007)    atoms: &[Atom],
[2008](https://docs.rs#2008)    indent: usize,
[2009](https://docs.rs#2009)    cfg: &FmtConfig,
[2010](https://docs.rs#2010)    tw: usize,
[2011](https://docs.rs#2011)    unit: &str,
[2012](https://docs.rs#2012)) -> Option<String> {
[2013](https://docs.rs#2013)    let (pre_end, suf_start) = expression_span(atoms)?;
[2014](https://docs.rs#2014)    if pre_end >= suf_start {
[2015](https://docs.rs#2015)        return None;
[2016](https://docs.rs#2016)    }
[2017](https://docs.rs#2017)    let expr = strip_redundant_parens(&atoms[pre_end..suf_start]);
[2018](https://docs.rs#2018)    let ops = top_level_binary_ops(expr);
[2019](https://docs.rs#2019)    let min_prec = ops.iter().map(|&(_, p)| p).min()?;
[2020](https://docs.rs#2020)    let prefix = flat_atoms(&atoms[..pre_end]);
[2021](https://docs.rs#2021)    let suffix = flat_atoms(&atoms[suf_start..]);
[2022](https://docs.rs#2022)    let lead = |out: &mut String| {
[2023](https://docs.rs#2023)        out.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent));
[2024](https://docs.rs#2024)        out.push_str(&prefix);
[2025](https://docs.rs#2025)        if !prefix.is_empty() {
[2026](https://docs.rs#2026)            out.push(' ');
[2027](https://docs.rs#2027)        }
[2028](https://docs.rs#2028)        out.push_str("(\n");
[2029](https://docs.rs#2029)    };
[2030](https://docs.rs#2030)    // Compact first: the whole expression on one indented continuation line (gdformat tries this
[2031](https://docs.rs#2031)    // before breaking — e.g. `(...).normalized() * power` that fits stays on one line).
[2032](https://docs.rs#2032)    let expr_flat = flat_atoms(expr);
[2033](https://docs.rs#2033)    if (indent + 1) * tw + cols(&expr_flat) <= cfg.line_width {
[2034](https://docs.rs#2034)        let mut out = String::new();
[2035](https://docs.rs#2035)        lead(&mut out);
[2036](https://docs.rs#2036)        out.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent + 1));
[2037](https://docs.rs#2037)        out.push_str(&expr_flat);
[2038](https://docs.rs#2038)        out.push('\n');
[2039](https://docs.rs#2039)        out.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent));
[2040](https://docs.rs#2040)        out.push(')');
[2041](https://docs.rs#2041)        out.push_str(&suffix);
[2042](https://docs.rs#2042)        return Some(out);
[2043](https://docs.rs#2043)    }
[2044](https://docs.rs#2044)
[2045](https://docs.rs#2045)    let split: Vec<usize> = ops
[2046](https://docs.rs#2046)        .iter()
[2047](https://docs.rs#2047)        .filter(|&&(_, p)| p == min_prec)
[2048](https://docs.rs#2048)        .map(|&(i, _)| i)
[2049](https://docs.rs#2049)        .collect();
[2050](https://docs.rs#2050)
[2051](https://docs.rs#2051)    // Build (leading-operator, operand-atoms) segments; the operator leads its following operand.
[2052](https://docs.rs#2052)    let mut segs: Vec<(Option<&str>, &[Atom])> = Vec::new();
[2053](https://docs.rs#2053)    let mut start = 0;
[2054](https://docs.rs#2054)    let mut prev_op: Option<&str> = None;
[2055](https://docs.rs#2055)    for &oi in &split {
[2056](https://docs.rs#2056)        segs.push((prev_op, &expr[start..oi]));
[2057](https://docs.rs#2057)        prev_op = Some(expr[oi].text.as_str());
[2058](https://docs.rs#2058)        start = oi + 1;
[2059](https://docs.rs#2059)    }
[2060](https://docs.rs#2060)    segs.push((prev_op, &expr[start..]));
[2061](https://docs.rs#2061)
[2062](https://docs.rs#2062)    let mut out = String::new();
[2063](https://docs.rs#2063)    lead(&mut out);
[2064](https://docs.rs#2064)    for (op, operand) in &segs {
[2065](https://docs.rs#2065)        out.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent + 1));
[2066](https://docs.rs#2066)        let mut col = (indent + 1) * tw;
[2067](https://docs.rs#2067)        if let Some(op) = op {
[2068](https://docs.rs#2068)            out.push_str(op);
[2069](https://docs.rs#2069)            out.push(' ');
[2070](https://docs.rs#2070)            col += cols(op) + 1;
[2071](https://docs.rs#2071)        }
[2072](https://docs.rs#2072)        let (od, _) = build_elems(operand, &mut 0, None);
[2073](https://docs.rs#2073)        if let Some(seq) = od.first() {
[2074](https://docs.rs#2074)            let (r, _) = render_seq(seq, indent + 1, col, cfg, tw, unit);
[2075](https://docs.rs#2075)            out.push_str(&r);
[2076](https://docs.rs#2076)        }
[2077](https://docs.rs#2077)        out.push('\n');
[2078](https://docs.rs#2078)    }
[2079](https://docs.rs#2079)    out.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent));
[2080](https://docs.rs#2080)    out.push(')');
[2081](https://docs.rs#2081)    out.push_str(&suffix);
[2082](https://docs.rs#2082)    Some(out)
[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)}
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)/// Wrap the statement's expression in injected parens on a single indented continuation line (the
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)/// **compact** form gdformat uses for a too-long expression with no top-level binary operator — e.g.
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)/// a long method chain). `None` if there is no such expression, it has a top-level operator (handled
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)/// by [`operator_chain_wrap`]), or even the compact line would still overflow.
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)fn compact_paren_wrap(
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)    atoms: &[Atom],
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)    indent: usize,
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)    cfg: &FmtConfig,
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)    tw: usize,
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)    unit: &str,
[2095](https://docs.rs#2095)) -> Option<String> {
[2096](https://docs.rs#2096)    let (pre_end, suf_start) = expression_span(atoms)?;
[2097](https://docs.rs#2097)    let expr = strip_redundant_parens(atoms.get(pre_end..suf_start)?);
[2098](https://docs.rs#2098)    // Only wrap an expression that has a bracketed group (e.g. a method chain) and no top-level
[2099](https://docs.rs#2099)    // binary operator: a bare expression / node-path is left on one line, as gdformat does.
[2100](https://docs.rs#2100)    if expr.is_empty()
[2101](https://docs.rs#2101)        || !top_level_binary_ops(expr).is_empty()
[2102](https://docs.rs#2102)        || !expr.iter().any(|a| open_close(&a.text).is_some())
[2103](https://docs.rs#2103)    {
[2104](https://docs.rs#2104)        return None;
[2105](https://docs.rs#2105)    }
[2106](https://docs.rs#2106)    let expr_flat = flat_atoms(expr);
[2107](https://docs.rs#2107)    if (indent + 1) * tw + cols(&expr_flat) > cfg.line_width {
[2108](https://docs.rs#2108)        return None;
[2109](https://docs.rs#2109)    }
[2110](https://docs.rs#2110)    let prefix = flat_atoms(&atoms[..pre_end]);
[2111](https://docs.rs#2111)    let suffix = flat_atoms(&atoms[suf_start..]);
[2112](https://docs.rs#2112)    let mut out = String::new();
[2113](https://docs.rs#2113)    out.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent));
[2114](https://docs.rs#2114)    out.push_str(&prefix);
[2115](https://docs.rs#2115)    if !prefix.is_empty() {
[2116](https://docs.rs#2116)        out.push(' ');
[2117](https://docs.rs#2117)    }
[2118](https://docs.rs#2118)    out.push_str("(\n");
[2119](https://docs.rs#2119)    out.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent + 1));
[2120](https://docs.rs#2120)    out.push_str(&expr_flat);
[2121](https://docs.rs#2121)    out.push('\n');
[2122](https://docs.rs#2122)    out.push_str(&unit.repeat(indent));
[2123](https://docs.rs#2123)    out.push(')');
[2124](https://docs.rs#2124)    out.push_str(&suffix);
[2125](https://docs.rs#2125)    Some(out)

[2128](https://docs.rs#2128)/// Collapse a (possibly multi-line) statement to its canonical single-line body — re-synthesising the
[2129](https://docs.rs#2129)/// inter-token spacing from scratch (so an already-wrapped statement is flattened). Returns `None`
[2130](https://docs.rs#2130)/// when the statement must be kept **verbatim**: it contains a comment, a multi-line lambda body, a
[2131](https://docs.rs#2131)/// backslash continuation, or a multi-line string (whose own newlines must be preserved).
[2132](https://docs.rs#2132)/// Whether a multi-line statement that could not be flattened to one line is safe to re-lay-out via
[2133](https://docs.rs#2133)/// the CST wrapper. It must (a) carry no comment — the wrapper does not thread comments through — and
[2134](https://docs.rs#2134)/// (b) contain a lambda, the one legitimate reason a statement cannot collapse to a single line (so we
[2135](https://docs.rs#2135)/// leave a multi-line string or an already-wrapped plain call verbatim). A leading `func`/`static func`
[2136](https://docs.rs#2136)/// is a function *declaration* header (its `func` is not a lambda), so it is excluded.
[2137](https://docs.rs#2137)fn stmt_is_rewrappable_multiline(stmt: &str) -> bool {
[2138](https://docs.rs#2138)    let toks = gdscript_syntax::tokenize(stmt);
[2139](https://docs.rs#2139)    let lead = stmt.trim_start();
[2140](https://docs.rs#2140)    let lead = lead.strip_prefix("static ").unwrap_or(lead);
[2141](https://docs.rs#2141)    if lead.starts_with("func ") || lead.starts_with("func(") {
[2142](https://docs.rs#2142)        return false; // a function *declaration* header, not a lambda expression
[2143](https://docs.rs#2143)    }
[2144](https://docs.rs#2144)    // The three legitimate reasons a statement cannot collapse onto one physical line and is still
[2145](https://docs.rs#2145)    // worth re-laying-out: it carries a lambda, a comment, or a multi-line string (the CST wrapper
[2146](https://docs.rs#2146)    // now threads all three; the meaning / comment-multiset nets fall back to verbatim otherwise).
[2147](https://docs.rs#2147)    let has_lambda = toks.iter().any(|t| t.kind == SyntaxKind::FuncKw);
[2148](https://docs.rs#2148)    let has_comment = toks.iter().any(|t| {
[2149](https://docs.rs#2149)        matches!(
[2150](https://docs.rs#2150)            t.kind,
[2151](https://docs.rs#2151)            SyntaxKind::LineComment
[2152](https://docs.rs#2152)                | SyntaxKind::DocComment
[2153](https://docs.rs#2153)                | SyntaxKind::RegionComment
[2154](https://docs.rs#2154)                | SyntaxKind::EndRegionComment
[2155](https://docs.rs#2155)        )
[2156](https://docs.rs#2156)    });
[2157](https://docs.rs#2157)    let has_multiline_string = toks
[2158](https://docs.rs#2158)        .iter()
[2159](https://docs.rs#2159)        .any(|t| t.kind == SyntaxKind::String && stmt[t.range].contains('\n'));
[2160](https://docs.rs#2160)    has_lambda || has_comment || has_multiline_string
[2161](https://docs.rs#2161)}
[2162](https://docs.rs#2162)
[2163](https://docs.rs#2163)fn flatten_statement(stmt: &str) -> Option<String> {
[2164](https://docs.rs#2164)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[2165](https://docs.rs#2165)    let raw = gdscript_syntax::tokenize(stmt);
[2166](https://docs.rs#2166)    let (toks, _diags) = gdscript_syntax::run_prepass(&raw, stmt);
[2167](https://docs.rs#2167)    let mut out = String::with_capacity(stmt.len());
[2168](https://docs.rs#2168)    let mut stack: Vec<S> = Vec::new();
[2169](https://docs.rs#2169)    let mut brace_enum: Vec<bool> = Vec::new();
[2170](https://docs.rs#2170)    let mut pending_enum = false;
[2171](https://docs.rs#2171)    let mut prev_sig: Option<S> = None;
[2172](https://docs.rs#2172)    let mut prev_unary = false;
[2173](https://docs.rs#2173)    let mut node_path = false;
[2174](https://docs.rs#2174)    let mut pending_break = false; // a line break was seen; the next token re-spaces across it
[2175](https://docs.rs#2175)    for t in &toks {
[2176](https://docs.rs#2176)        match t.kind {
[2177](https://docs.rs#2177)            S::NewlinePhys => pending_break = true,
[2178](https://docs.rs#2178)            // A synthetic newline inside brackets is a multi-line lambda body — cannot collapse.
[2179](https://docs.rs#2179)            S::Newline if !stack.is_empty() => return None,
[2180](https://docs.rs#2180)            S::Indent | S::Dedent | S::Bom | S::Newline => {}
[2181](https://docs.rs#2181)            // A backslash line continuation is collapsed away: trim the space before the `\` so the
[2182](https://docs.rs#2182)            // join is not double-spaced; the following physical newline then sets `pending_break` and
[2183](https://docs.rs#2183)            // the next token re-spaces once (and the statement is later re-wrapped) like gdformat,
[2184](https://docs.rs#2184)            // which converts `\`-continued statements to paren-wrapped multi-line form.
[2185](https://docs.rs#2185)            S::LineContinuation => trim_trailing_inline_ws(&mut out),
[2186](https://docs.rs#2186)            S::Whitespace => {
[2187](https://docs.rs#2187)                // Keep intra-line spacing verbatim (it is already canonical / the user's, when
[2188](https://docs.rs#2188)                // spacing-normalisation is off); drop a line's leading indentation.
[2189](https://docs.rs#2189)                if !pending_break && prev_sig.is_some() {
[2190](https://docs.rs#2190)                    out.push_str(&stmt[t.range]);
[2191](https://docs.rs#2191)                }
[2192](https://docs.rs#2192)            }
[2193](https://docs.rs#2193)            S::LineComment | S::DocComment | S::RegionComment | S::EndRegionComment => return None,
[2194](https://docs.rs#2194)            k => {
[2195](https://docs.rs#2195)                let text = &stmt[t.range];
[2196](https://docs.rs#2196)                if matches!(k, S::String | S::StringName | S::NodePath) && text.contains('\n') {
[2197](https://docs.rs#2197)                    return None; // a multi-line string — keep the statement verbatim
[2198](https://docs.rs#2198)                }
[2199](https://docs.rs#2199)                // Replace a line break by the spacing the intra-line rules would synthesize.
[2200](https://docs.rs#2200)                if pending_break {
[2201](https://docs.rs#2201)                    let sp = match prev_sig {
[2202](https://docs.rs#2202)                        Some(_) if node_path && matches!(k, S::Ident | S::Slash | S::String) => {
[2203](https://docs.rs#2203)                            Spacing::Verbatim
[2204](https://docs.rs#2204)                        }
[2205](https://docs.rs#2205)                        Some(p) => {
[2206](https://docs.rs#2206)                            let top_enum = stack.last() == Some(&S::LBrace)
[2207](https://docs.rs#2207)                                && brace_enum.last() == Some(&true);
[2208](https://docs.rs#2208)                            space_before(p, k, stack.last().copied(), prev_unary, top_enum)
[2209](https://docs.rs#2209)                        }
[2210](https://docs.rs#2210)                        None => Spacing::None,
[2211](https://docs.rs#2211)                    };
[2212](https://docs.rs#2212)                    if matches!(sp, Spacing::Single) {
[2213](https://docs.rs#2213)                        out.push(' ');
[2214](https://docs.rs#2214)                    }
[2215](https://docs.rs#2215)                    pending_break = false;
[2216](https://docs.rs#2216)                }
[2217](https://docs.rs#2217)                out.push_str(text);
[2218](https://docs.rs#2218)                match k {
[2219](https://docs.rs#2219)                    S::LBrace => {
[2220](https://docs.rs#2220)                        stack.push(k);
[2221](https://docs.rs#2221)                        brace_enum.push(pending_enum);
[2222](https://docs.rs#2222)                        pending_enum = false;
[2223](https://docs.rs#2223)                    }
[2224](https://docs.rs#2224)                    S::LParen | S::LBrack => stack.push(k),
[2225](https://docs.rs#2225)                    S::RBrace => {
[2226](https://docs.rs#2226)                        stack.pop();
[2227](https://docs.rs#2227)                        brace_enum.pop();
[2228](https://docs.rs#2228)                    }
[2229](https://docs.rs#2229)                    S::RParen | S::RBrack => {
[2230](https://docs.rs#2230)                        stack.pop();
[2231](https://docs.rs#2231)                    }
[2232](https://docs.rs#2232)                    _ => {}
[2233](https://docs.rs#2233)                }
[2234](https://docs.rs#2234)                if k == S::EnumKw {
[2235](https://docs.rs#2235)                    pending_enum = true;
[2236](https://docs.rs#2236)                }
[2237](https://docs.rs#2237)                let unary_ctx = prev_sig.is_none_or(|p| !is_operand_end(p));
[2238](https://docs.rs#2238)                if k == S::Dollar || (k == S::Percent && unary_ctx) {
[2239](https://docs.rs#2239)                    node_path = true;
[2240](https://docs.rs#2240)                } else if node_path && !matches!(k, S::Ident | S::Slash | S::String) {
[2241](https://docs.rs#2241)                    node_path = false;
[2242](https://docs.rs#2242)                }
[2243](https://docs.rs#2243)                prev_unary = match k {
[2244](https://docs.rs#2244)                    S::Minus | S::Plus => unary_ctx,
[2245](https://docs.rs#2245)                    S::Tilde | S::Bang => true,
[2246](https://docs.rs#2246)                    _ => false,
[2247](https://docs.rs#2247)                };
[2248](https://docs.rs#2248)                prev_sig = Some(k);
[2249](https://docs.rs#2249)            }
[2250](https://docs.rs#2250)        }
[2251](https://docs.rs#2251)    }
[2252](https://docs.rs#2252)    Some(out)
[2253](https://docs.rs#2253)}

[2255](https://docs.rs#2255)/// Render a flattened statement `body` at `indent` into its canonical layout — flat if it fits, else
[2256](https://docs.rs#2256)/// wrapped (operator-chain → bracketed compact/exploded → compact-paren). Always indented.
[2257](https://docs.rs#2257)fn render_statement(body: &str, indent: usize, cfg: &FmtConfig, tw: usize, unit: &str) -> String {
[2258](https://docs.rs#2258)    // Primary path: gdformat's own algorithm, driven from the CST (see `wrap`). It owns the layout and
[2259](https://docs.rs#2259)    // is faithful to gdformat. `wrap::render` self-validates that its output is meaning-equivalent to
[2260](https://docs.rs#2260)    // the body (allowing exactly gdformat's legitimate rewrites — redundant grouping parens, trailing
[2261](https://docs.rs#2261)    // commas, string quotes); it returns `None` otherwise, and we fall back to the heuristic below.
[2262](https://docs.rs#2262)    if let Some(out) = wrap::render(body, indent, cfg) {
[2263](https://docs.rs#2263)        return out;
[2264](https://docs.rs#2264)    }
[2265](https://docs.rs#2265)    let flat = || format!("{}{body}", unit.repeat(indent));
[2266](https://docs.rs#2266)    let Some(atoms) = line_atoms(body) else {
[2267](https://docs.rs#2267)        return flat();
[2268](https://docs.rs#2268)    };
[2269](https://docs.rs#2269)    let width = indent * tw + cols(body);
[2270](https://docs.rs#2270)    // A too-long top-level binary-operator chain is wrapped in injected parens (highest priority).
[2271](https://docs.rs#2271)    if width > cfg.line_width {
[2272](https://docs.rs#2272)        let oc = operator_chain_wrap(&atoms, indent, cfg, tw, unit);
[2273](https://docs.rs#2273)        if let Some(oc) = oc {
[2274](https://docs.rs#2274)            return oc;
[2275](https://docs.rs#2275)        }
[2276](https://docs.rs#2276)    }
[2277](https://docs.rs#2277)    if !atoms.iter().any(|a| open_close(&a.text).is_some()) {
[2278](https://docs.rs#2278)        return flat();
[2279](https://docs.rs#2279)    }
[2280](https://docs.rs#2280)    let (docs, _) = build_elems(&atoms, &mut 0, None);
[2281](https://docs.rs#2281)    if docs.len() != 1 {
[2282](https://docs.rs#2282)        return flat();
[2283](https://docs.rs#2283)    }
[2284](https://docs.rs#2284)    let top = &docs[0];
[2285](https://docs.rs#2285)    // Faithfulness: the atom tree must round-trip the body's *tokens* (spacing may differ — e.g. enum
[2286](https://docs.rs#2286)    // braces / type-annotation colons — which `flat_seq` does not reproduce).
[2287](https://docs.rs#2287)    if !same_significant_tokens(&flat_seq(top), body) {
[2288](https://docs.rs#2288)        return flat();
[2289](https://docs.rs#2289)    }
[2290](https://docs.rs#2290)    // Stay flat unless the line is too long or a magic trailing comma forces it exploded.
[2291](https://docs.rs#2291)    let forced = top
[2292](https://docs.rs#2292)        .iter()
[2293](https://docs.rs#2293)        .any(|d| matches!(d, ReflowDoc::Group { elems, magic, .. } if group_forced(elems, *magic)));
[2294](https://docs.rs#2294)    if width <= cfg.line_width && !forced {
[2295](https://docs.rs#2295)        return flat();
[2296](https://docs.rs#2296)    }
[2297](https://docs.rs#2297)    let (rendered, _) = render_seq(top, indent, indent * tw, cfg, tw, unit);
[2298](https://docs.rs#2298)    let result = format!("{}{rendered}", unit.repeat(indent));
[2299](https://docs.rs#2299)    // If bracket reflow still overflows (e.g. a long method chain), wrap the expression compact.
[2300](https://docs.rs#2300)    let overflows = result.lines().any(|l| display_cols(l, tw) > cfg.line_width);
[2301](https://docs.rs#2301)    if overflows {
[2302](https://docs.rs#2302)        let cp = compact_paren_wrap(&atoms, indent, cfg, tw, unit);
[2303](https://docs.rs#2303)        if let Some(cp) = cp {
[2304](https://docs.rs#2304)            return cp;
[2305](https://docs.rs#2305)        }
[2306](https://docs.rs#2306)    }
[2307](https://docs.rs#2307)    result
[2308](https://docs.rs#2308)}
[2309](https://docs.rs#2309)
[2310](https://docs.rs#2310)/// Re-flow the layout of every statement: a statement that now fits is collapsed onto one line, one
[2311](https://docs.rs#2311)/// that does not is re-wrapped to its canonical form — gdformat-style layout ownership. Statements
[2312](https://docs.rs#2312)/// that cannot be safely collapsed (comments, multi-line lambdas, multi-line strings) are preserved.
[2313](https://docs.rs#2313)/// Token-preserving (modulo the trailing commas / parens the meaning-equivalence net allows).
[2314](https://docs.rs#2314)#[allow(
[2315](https://docs.rs#2315)    clippy::too_many_lines,
[2316](https://docs.rs#2316)    reason = "one cohesive pass: per-line bracket/straddle bookkeeping then logical-statement grouping"
[2317](https://docs.rs#2317))]
[2318](https://docs.rs#2318)fn reflow(formatted: &str, config: &FmtConfig) -> String {
[2319](https://docs.rs#2319)    use SyntaxKind as S;
[2320](https://docs.rs#2320)    if config.line_width == 0 {
[2321](https://docs.rs#2321)        return formatted.to_owned();
[2322](https://docs.rs#2322)    }
[2323](https://docs.rs#2323)    let tw = if config.use_tabs {
[2324](https://docs.rs#2324)        4
[2325](https://docs.rs#2325)    } else {
[2326](https://docs.rs#2326)        config.indent_size.max(1)
[2327](https://docs.rs#2327)    };
[2328](https://docs.rs#2328)    let unit = config.indent_unit();
[2329](https://docs.rs#2329)    let lines: Vec<&str> = formatted.split('\n').collect();
[2330](https://docs.rs#2330)
[2331](https://docs.rs#2331)    let line_starts: Vec<usize> = std::iter::once(0)
[2332](https://docs.rs#2332)        .chain(
[2333](https://docs.rs#2333)            formatted
[2334](https://docs.rs#2334)                .bytes()
[2335](https://docs.rs#2335)                .enumerate()
[2336](https://docs.rs#2336)                .filter_map(|(i, b)| (b == b'\n').then_some(i + 1)),
[2337](https://docs.rs#2337)        )
[2338](https://docs.rs#2338)        .collect();
[2339](https://docs.rs#2339)    let line_of = |off: usize| line_starts.partition_point(|&s| s <= off).saturating_sub(1);
[2340](https://docs.rs#2340)
[2341](https://docs.rs#2341)    // Per line: bracket depth at its start, whether a multi-line token (e.g. a `"""..."""` string)
[2342](https://docs.rs#2342)    // covers it, and whether it ends in a `\` continuation — used to group physical lines into the
[2343](https://docs.rs#2343)    // logical statement they belong to.
[2344](https://docs.rs#2344)    let raw = gdscript_syntax::tokenize(formatted);
[2345](https://docs.rs#2345)    let mut start_depth = vec![i32::MIN; lines.len()];
[2346](https://docs.rs#2346)    let mut straddled = vec![false; lines.len()];
[2347](https://docs.rs#2347)    let mut ends_cont = vec![false; lines.len()];
[2348](https://docs.rs#2348)    let mut depth: i32 = 0;
[2349](https://docs.rs#2349)    for t in &raw {
[2350](https://docs.rs#2350)        let s = usize::from(t.range.start());
[2351](https://docs.rs#2351)        let e = usize::from(t.range.end()).saturating_sub(1).max(s);
[2352](https://docs.rs#2352)        let (sl, el) = (line_of(s), line_of(e));
[2353](https://docs.rs#2353)        if sl < start_depth.len() && start_depth[sl] == i32::MIN {
[2354](https://docs.rs#2354)            start_depth[sl] = depth;
[2355](https://docs.rs#2355)        }
[2356](https://docs.rs#2356)        if el > sl {
[2357](https://docs.rs#2357)            let end = el.min(lines.len().saturating_sub(1));
[2358](https://docs.rs#2358)            straddled[sl..=end].fill(true);
[2359](https://docs.rs#2359)        }
[2360](https://docs.rs#2360)        match t.kind {
[2361](https://docs.rs#2361)            S::LParen | S::LBrack | S::LBrace => depth += 1,
[2362](https://docs.rs#2362)            S::RParen | S::RBrack | S::RBrace => depth -= 1,
[2363](https://docs.rs#2363)            S::LineContinuation if sl < ends_cont.len() => ends_cont[sl] = true,
[2364](https://docs.rs#2364)            // The next line starts at the current depth — covers blank lines (which have no token of
[2365](https://docs.rs#2365)            // their own to set `start_depth`, so they would otherwise stay unset and be absorbed).
[2366](https://docs.rs#2366)            S::NewlinePhys if sl + 1 < start_depth.len() && start_depth[sl + 1] == i32::MIN => {
[2367](https://docs.rs#2367)                start_depth[sl + 1] = depth;
[2368](https://docs.rs#2368)            }
[2369](https://docs.rs#2369)            _ => {}
[2370](https://docs.rs#2370)        }
[2371](https://docs.rs#2371)    }
[2372](https://docs.rs#2372)    let sd = |i: usize| {
[2373](https://docs.rs#2373)        let d = start_depth.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0);
[2374](https://docs.rs#2374)        if d == i32::MIN { 0 } else { d }
[2375](https://docs.rs#2375)    };
[2376](https://docs.rs#2376)    let strad = |i: usize| straddled.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(false);
[2377](https://docs.rs#2377)    let cont = |i: usize| ends_cont.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(false);
[2378](https://docs.rs#2378)
[2379](https://docs.rs#2379)    let mut out = String::with_capacity(formatted.len());
[2380](https://docs.rs#2380)    let mut li = 0;
[2381](https://docs.rs#2381)    while li < lines.len() {
[2382](https://docs.rs#2382)        let line = lines[li];
[2383](https://docs.rs#2383)        // A statement head: a non-blank line at bracket depth 0 that is not the continuation of the
[2384](https://docs.rs#2384)        // previous line (a `\` or a multi-line token spanning the boundary).
[2385](https://docs.rs#2385)        let head = !line.trim().is_empty()
[2386](https://docs.rs#2386)            && sd(li) == 0
[2387](https://docs.rs#2387)            && (li == 0 || !cont(li - 1))
[2388](https://docs.rs#2388)            && !(li > 0 && strad(li) && strad(li - 1));
[2389](https://docs.rs#2389)        if !head {
[2390](https://docs.rs#2390)            out.push_str(line);
[2391](https://docs.rs#2391)            if li + 1 < lines.len() {
[2392](https://docs.rs#2392)                out.push('\n');
[2393](https://docs.rs#2393)            }
[2394](https://docs.rs#2394)            li += 1;
[2395](https://docs.rs#2395)            continue;
[2396](https://docs.rs#2396)        }
[2397](https://docs.rs#2397)        // Extend to the end of the logical statement (brackets open, a multi-line token spanning the
[2398](https://docs.rs#2398)        // boundary, or a backslash continuation).
[2399](https://docs.rs#2399)        let mut j = li;
[2400](https://docs.rs#2400)        while j + 1 < lines.len() && (sd(j + 1) != 0 || (strad(j) && strad(j + 1)) || cont(j)) {
[2401](https://docs.rs#2401)            j += 1;
[2402](https://docs.rs#2402)        }
[2403](https://docs.rs#2403)        let stmt = lines[li..=j].join("\n");
[2404](https://docs.rs#2404)        let indent = if config.use_tabs {
[2405](https://docs.rs#2405)            line.bytes().take_while(|&b| b == b'\t').count()
[2406](https://docs.rs#2406)        } else {
[2407](https://docs.rs#2407)            line.bytes()
[2408](https://docs.rs#2408)                .take_while(|&b| b == b' ')
[2409](https://docs.rs#2409)                .count()
[2410](https://docs.rs#2410)                .checked_div(config.indent_size)
[2411](https://docs.rs#2411)                .unwrap_or(0)
[2412](https://docs.rs#2412)        };
[2413](https://docs.rs#2413)        let rendered = match flatten_statement(&stmt) {
[2414](https://docs.rs#2414)            Some(body) => Some(render_statement(&body, indent, config, tw, &unit)),
[2415](https://docs.rs#2415)            // A statement that cannot be collapsed onto one physical line *because it carries a
[2416](https://docs.rs#2416)            // multi-line lambda body* (a compound- or multi-statement-bodied lambda argument) is still
[2417](https://docs.rs#2417)            // re-laid-out by the CST wrapper directly, from its dedented multi-line form — gdformat
[2418](https://docs.rs#2418)            // reformats *every* statement, not just single-line ones. We only attempt this for a
[2419](https://docs.rs#2419)            // comment-free lambda-bearing statement (the wrapper does not carry comments through, and a
[2420](https://docs.rs#2420)            // plain multi-line string / already-wrapped statement is better left verbatim); the wrapper
[2421](https://docs.rs#2421)            // still self-validates meaning-equivalence and returns `None` (→ verbatim) otherwise.
[2422](https://docs.rs#2422)            None if stmt_is_rewrappable_multiline(&stmt) => {
[2423](https://docs.rs#2423)                wrap::render(&wrap::dedent(&stmt), indent, config)
[2424](https://docs.rs#2424)            }
[2425](https://docs.rs#2425)            None => None,
[2426](https://docs.rs#2426)        };
[2427](https://docs.rs#2427)        out.push_str(rendered.as_deref().unwrap_or(&stmt));
[2428](https://docs.rs#2428)        if j + 1 < lines.len() {
[2429](https://docs.rs#2429)            out.push('\n');
[2430](https://docs.rs#2430)        }
[2431](https://docs.rs#2431)        li = j + 1;
[2432](https://docs.rs#2432)    }
[2433](https://docs.rs#2433)    out
[2434](https://docs.rs#2434)}
[2435](https://docs.rs#2435)
[2436](https://docs.rs#2436)/// Trim trailing spaces/tabs from the end of `out` (the current line).
[2437](https://docs.rs#2437)fn trim_trailing_inline_ws(out: &mut String) {
[2438](https://docs.rs#2438)    while out.ends_with(' ') || out.ends_with('\t') {
[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)        out.pop();
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)    }

[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)/// Whether two sources lex to the same sequence of significant (non-trivia) tokens — a
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)/// spacing-insensitive equality used by the reflow faithfulness check and the token-preserving tests.
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)fn same_significant_tokens(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)    fn sig(s: &str) -> Vec<(SyntaxKind, &str)> {
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)        gdscript_syntax::tokenize(s)
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)            .into_iter()
[2449](https://docs.rs#2449)            // A `;` is a statement separator equivalent to a newline — ignore it, so splitting
[2450](https://docs.rs#2450)            // `a; b` onto two lines is recognised as token-preserving.
[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)            .filter(|t| !t.kind.is_trivia() && t.kind != SyntaxKind::Semicolon)
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)            .map(|t| (t.kind, &s[t.range]))
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)            .collect()
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)    }
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)    sig(a) == sig(b)
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)}
[2457](https://docs.rs#2457)
[2458](https://docs.rs#2458)/// Re-emit a string-literal token's text in gdformat's canonical quote style: prefer `"`, fall back
[2459](https://docs.rs#2459)/// to `'` only when the body has more `"` than `'` (fewer escapes), keeping the prefix (`r`/`&`/`^`)
[2460](https://docs.rs#2460)/// and the decoded value. Idempotent. Triple-quoted strings are left verbatim (rare; not normalized).
[2461](https://docs.rs#2461)pub(crate) fn canonical_string(text: &str) -> String {
[2462](https://docs.rs#2462)    let Some(qpos) = text.find(['"', '\'']) else {
[2463](https://docs.rs#2463)        return text.to_owned(); // defensive: not actually a string literal
[2464](https://docs.rs#2464)    };
[2465](https://docs.rs#2465)    let prefix = &text[..qpos];
[2466](https://docs.rs#2466)    let rest = &text[qpos..];
[2467](https://docs.rs#2467)    let rb = rest.as_bytes();
[2468](https://docs.rs#2468)    let quote = rb[0];
[2469](https://docs.rs#2469)    // Triple-quoted. gdformat converts a *single-line* triple-**single**-quoted string (`'''…'''`)
[2470](https://docs.rs#2470)    // to a regular string (strip the outer `''` and apply the regular quote rule to `'…'`); a
[2471](https://docs.rs#2471)    // triple-**double** (`"""…"""`) and any *multi-line* triple-quoted string are left verbatim.
[2472](https://docs.rs#2472)    if rb.len() >= 6 && rb[1] == quote && rb[2] == quote {
[2473](https://docs.rs#2473)        if quote == b'\'' && rest.ends_with("'''") {
[2474](https://docs.rs#2474)            let body = &rest[3..rest.len() - 3];
[2475](https://docs.rs#2475)            if !body.contains('\n') {
[2476](https://docs.rs#2476)                return canonical_string(&format!("{prefix}'{body}'"));
[2477](https://docs.rs#2477)            }
[2478](https://docs.rs#2478)        }
[2479](https://docs.rs#2479)        return text.to_owned();
[2480](https://docs.rs#2480)    }
[2481](https://docs.rs#2481)    if rest.len() < 2 || rb[rest.len() - 1] != quote {
[2482](https://docs.rs#2482)        return text.to_owned(); // unterminated / malformed: don't touch
[2483](https://docs.rs#2483)    }
[2484](https://docs.rs#2484)    let body = &rest[1..rest.len() - 1];
[2485](https://docs.rs#2485)    // Raw strings (`r"..."`) cannot escape — only switch quotes if the body lacks the target.
[2486](https://docs.rs#2486)    if prefix.contains('r') {
[2487](https://docs.rs#2487)        let target = if !body.contains('"') {
[2488](https://docs.rs#2488)            '"'
[2489](https://docs.rs#2489)        } else if !body.contains('\'') {
[2490](https://docs.rs#2490)            '\''
[2491](https://docs.rs#2491)        } else {
[2492](https://docs.rs#2492)            quote as char
[2493](https://docs.rs#2493)        };
[2494](https://docs.rs#2494)        return format!("{prefix}{target}{body}{target}");
[2495](https://docs.rs#2495)    }
[2496](https://docs.rs#2496)    // Parse the body into units (escaped or literal) and count the value's quote characters.
[2497](https://docs.rs#2497)    let mut units: Vec<(bool, char)> = Vec::new();
[2498](https://docs.rs#2498)    let (mut dq, mut sq) = (0usize, 0usize);
[2499](https://docs.rs#2499)    let mut chars = body.chars();
[2500](https://docs.rs#2500)    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
[2501](https://docs.rs#2501)        if c == '\\' {
[2502](https://docs.rs#2502)            if let Some(n) = chars.next() {
[2503](https://docs.rs#2503)                units.push((true, n));
[2504](https://docs.rs#2504)                match n {
[2505](https://docs.rs#2505)                    '"' => dq += 1,
[2506](https://docs.rs#2506)                    '\'' => sq += 1,
[2507](https://docs.rs#2507)                    _ => {}
[2508](https://docs.rs#2508)                }
[2509](https://docs.rs#2509)            } else {
[2510](https://docs.rs#2510)                units.push((false, '\\'));
[2511](https://docs.rs#2511)            }
[2512](https://docs.rs#2512)        } else {
[2513](https://docs.rs#2513)            units.push((false, c));
[2514](https://docs.rs#2514)            match c {
[2515](https://docs.rs#2515)                '"' => dq += 1,
[2516](https://docs.rs#2516)                '\'' => sq += 1,
[2517](https://docs.rs#2517)                _ => {}
[2518](https://docs.rs#2518)            }
[2519](https://docs.rs#2519)        }
[2520](https://docs.rs#2520)    }
[2521](https://docs.rs#2521)    let target = if dq > sq { '\'' } else { '"' };
[2522](https://docs.rs#2522)    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
[2523](https://docs.rs#2523)    out.push_str(prefix);
[2524](https://docs.rs#2524)    out.push(target);
[2525](https://docs.rs#2525)    for (esc, c) in units {
[2526](https://docs.rs#2526)        if c == '"' || c == '\'' {
[2527](https://docs.rs#2527)            if c == target {
[2528](https://docs.rs#2528)                out.push('\\');
[2529](https://docs.rs#2529)            }
[2530](https://docs.rs#2530)            out.push(c);
[2531](https://docs.rs#2531)        } else {
[2532](https://docs.rs#2532)            if esc {
[2533](https://docs.rs#2533)                out.push('\\');
[2534](https://docs.rs#2534)            }
[2535](https://docs.rs#2535)            out.push(c);
[2536](https://docs.rs#2536)        }
[2537](https://docs.rs#2537)    }
[2538](https://docs.rs#2538)    out.push(target);
[2539](https://docs.rs#2539)    out
[2540](https://docs.rs#2540)}
[2541](https://docs.rs#2541)
[2542](https://docs.rs#2542)/// A normalised parse-tree event used by [`meaning_preserved`].
[2543](https://docs.rs#2543)#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
[2544](https://docs.rs#2544)enum TreeEvent {
[2545](https://docs.rs#2545)    Open(SyntaxKind),
[2546](https://docs.rs#2546)    Close,
[2547](https://docs.rs#2547)    Token(SyntaxKind, String),
[2548](https://docs.rs#2548)}
[2549](https://docs.rs#2549)
[2550](https://docs.rs#2550)/// Walk a parse-tree node, appending normalised events: trivia is dropped, a `ParenExpr` is
[2551](https://docs.rs#2551)/// **unwrapped** (its node + `(`/`)` tokens removed, its inner expression spliced in — so a
[2552](https://docs.rs#2552)/// *redundant* grouping paren is invisible while a precedence-changing one still differs, because the
[2553](https://docs.rs#2553)/// surrounding `BinExpr` nesting changes), and string literals are recorded by canonical quote form.
[2554](https://docs.rs#2554)fn emit_tree_events(node: &gdscript_syntax::GdNode, out: &mut Vec<TreeEvent>) {
[2555](https://docs.rs#2555)    use cstree::util::NodeOrToken;
[2556](https://docs.rs#2556)    if node.kind() == SyntaxKind::ParenExpr {
[2557](https://docs.rs#2557)        for child in node.children() {
[2558](https://docs.rs#2558)            emit_tree_events(child, out);
[2559](https://docs.rs#2559)        }
[2560](https://docs.rs#2560)        return;
[2561](https://docs.rs#2561)    }
[2562](https://docs.rs#2562)    out.push(TreeEvent::Open(node.kind()));
[2563](https://docs.rs#2563)    for child in node.children_with_tokens() {
[2564](https://docs.rs#2564)        match child {
[2565](https://docs.rs#2565)            // An *empty* parameter list carries no meaning — `signal s()` ≡ `signal s` (a func always
[2566](https://docs.rs#2566)            // has `()`, so dropping the empty list uniformly leaves func headers unaffected). Skipping
[2567](https://docs.rs#2567)            // it here lets the formatter remove a signal's empty `()` without the net objecting.
[2568](https://docs.rs#2568)            NodeOrToken::Node(n)
[2569](https://docs.rs#2569)                if n.kind() == SyntaxKind::ParamList && n.children().next().is_none() => {}
[2570](https://docs.rs#2570)            NodeOrToken::Node(n) => emit_tree_events(n, out),
[2571](https://docs.rs#2571)            NodeOrToken::Token(t) => {
[2572](https://docs.rs#2572)                let kind = t.kind();
[2573](https://docs.rs#2573)                // Skip trivia, the synthetic block-structure markers (`Newline`/`Indent`/`Dedent` —
[2574](https://docs.rs#2574)                // the block nesting they encode is already captured by the surrounding node Open/Close
[2575](https://docs.rs#2575)                // events, and they differ between an inline and a multi-line form of the *same*
[2576](https://docs.rs#2576)                // construct, e.g. `func(): x` vs a wrapped lambda body), and a `;` statement separator.
[2577](https://docs.rs#2577)                if kind.is_trivia() || kind.is_synthetic_layout() || kind == SyntaxKind::Semicolon {
[2578](https://docs.rs#2578)                    continue;
[2579](https://docs.rs#2579)                }
[2580](https://docs.rs#2580)                let text = if matches!(
[2581](https://docs.rs#2581)                    kind,
[2582](https://docs.rs#2582)                    SyntaxKind::String | SyntaxKind::StringName | SyntaxKind::NodePath
[2583](https://docs.rs#2583)                ) {
[2584](https://docs.rs#2584)                    canonical_string(t.text())
[2585](https://docs.rs#2585)                } else {
[2586](https://docs.rs#2586)                    t.text().to_owned()
[2587](https://docs.rs#2587)                };
[2588](https://docs.rs#2588)                out.push(TreeEvent::Token(kind, text));
[2589](https://docs.rs#2589)            }
[2590](https://docs.rs#2590)        }
[2591](https://docs.rs#2591)    }
[2592](https://docs.rs#2592)    out.push(TreeEvent::Close);
[2593](https://docs.rs#2593)}
[2594](https://docs.rs#2594)
[2595](https://docs.rs#2595)/// Whether `a` and `b` are **meaning-equivalent** — the relaxed safety net used once the formatter
[2596](https://docs.rs#2596)/// performs token-*mutating* rewrites. It compares the **parse-tree structure** (so token order,
[2597](https://docs.rs#2597)/// nesting and operator precedence must all match), normalising away exactly the differences gdformat
[2598](https://docs.rs#2598)/// is allowed to introduce: **redundant grouping parens** are unwrapped, a **trailing comma** before a
[2599](https://docs.rs#2599)/// closing bracket is dropped, and **string literals are compared by canonical quote form**. A
[2600](https://docs.rs#2600)/// dropped/added/reordered token, a changed string *value*, or a precedence change is still caught.
[2601](https://docs.rs#2601)pub(crate) fn meaning_preserved(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
[2602](https://docs.rs#2602)    fn events(s: &str) -> Vec<TreeEvent> {
[2603](https://docs.rs#2603)        let mut raw = Vec::new();
[2604](https://docs.rs#2604)        emit_tree_events(&gdscript_syntax::parse(s).syntax_node(), &mut raw);
[2605](https://docs.rs#2605)        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(raw.len());
[2606](https://docs.rs#2606)        for i in 0..raw.len() {
[2607](https://docs.rs#2607)            // Drop a trailing comma (a `,` immediately before a closing-bracket token).
[2608](https://docs.rs#2608)            let trailing_comma = matches!(&raw[i], TreeEvent::Token(SyntaxKind::Comma, _))
[2609](https://docs.rs#2609)                && matches!(
[2610](https://docs.rs#2610)                    raw.get(i + 1),
[2611](https://docs.rs#2611)                    Some(TreeEvent::Token(
[2612](https://docs.rs#2612)                        SyntaxKind::RParen | SyntaxKind::RBrack | SyntaxKind::RBrace,
[2613](https://docs.rs#2613)                        _
[2614](https://docs.rs#2614)                    ))
[2615](https://docs.rs#2615)                );
[2616](https://docs.rs#2616)            if !trailing_comma {
[2617](https://docs.rs#2617)                out.push(raw[i].clone());
[2618](https://docs.rs#2618)            }
[2619](https://docs.rs#2619)        }
[2620](https://docs.rs#2620)        out
[2621](https://docs.rs#2621)    }
[2622](https://docs.rs#2622)    events(a) == events(b)
[2623](https://docs.rs#2623)}

[2691](https://docs.rs#2691)        // block. (Our paren-retention already matched gdformat; this closes the comment placement.)
[2692](https://docs.rs#2692)        let src = "func f():\n\tif (\n\t\t\t# on\n\t\t\taaa and bbb\n\t) or (\n\t\t\t# off\n\t\t\tccc and ddd\n\t):\n\t\tpass\n";
[2693](https://docs.rs#2693)        let out = fmt(src);
[2694](https://docs.rs#2694)        assert!(out.contains("(aaa and bbb)"), "operand 0 compacts:\n{out}");
[2695](https://docs.rs#2695)        assert!(
[2696](https://docs.rs#2696)            out.contains("or (ccc and ddd)"),
[2697](https://docs.rs#2697)            "operator leads the compacted operand 1:\n{out}"
[2698](https://docs.rs#2698)        );
[2699](https://docs.rs#2699)        assert!(
[2700](https://docs.rs#2700)            out.contains("# on") && out.contains("# off"),
[2701](https://docs.rs#2701)            "comments preserved:\n{out}"
[2702](https://docs.rs#2702)        );
[2703](https://docs.rs#2703)        // (No raw `same_significant_tokens` here: a multi-line operator chain is wrapped in an
[2704](https://docs.rs#2704)        // injected `(…)` — gdformat does the same, and the formatter's own net accounts for it, but a
[2705](https://docs.rs#2705)        // raw token compare would not. The byte-exact gdformat corpus parity is the real guard.)
[2706](https://docs.rs#2706)        assert_eq!(fmt(&out), out, "idempotent");
[2707](https://docs.rs#2707)    }

[2757](https://docs.rs#2757)    fn comment_between_statements_does_not_corrupt_the_next_line() {

[2765](https://docs.rs#2765)        );
[2766](https://docs.rs#2766)        assert!(
[2767](https://docs.rs#2767)            parses_clean(&out),
[2768](https://docs.rs#2768)            "formatter must not emit mixed indent: {out:?}"
[2769](https://docs.rs#2769)        );

[2774](https://docs.rs#2774)    fn leading_body_comment_is_indented_to_the_block() {
[2775](https://docs.rs#2775)        // A comment that is the FIRST line of a block: the prepass emits `Indent` only at the first
[2776](https://docs.rs#2776)        // *code* line, so the comment's raw depth is wrong — but it is re-indented to its intended
[2777](https://docs.rs#2777)        // block depth by comparing its authored indentation against the surrounding code lines
[2778](https://docs.rs#2778)        // (gdformat's rule). Works for the space-indented input here too (length comparison is
[2779](https://docs.rs#2779)        // indent-width agnostic).
[2780](https://docs.rs#2780)        let src = "func g():\n  # c\n  var x = 1\n  var y = 2\n";

[2783](https://docs.rs#2783)        assert!(parses_clean(&out), "{out:?}");
[2784](https://docs.rs#2784)        assert_eq!(fmt(&out), out, "must be idempotent");
[2785](https://docs.rs#2785)    }

[2808](https://docs.rs#2808)    // ---- Phase-4 increment A: intra-line spacing ----
[2809](https://docs.rs#2809)
[2810](https://docs.rs#2810)    /// Format a single statement inside a function body, returning just the (de-indented) body line.
[2811](https://docs.rs#2811)    /// Wrapping keeps `safe_mode` happy (a bare statement is not a valid top-level form).
[2812](https://docs.rs#2812)    fn fmt_stmt(stmt: &str) -> String {
[2813](https://docs.rs#2813)        let src = format!("func _f():\n\t{stmt}\n");
[2814](https://docs.rs#2814)        let out = fmt(&src);
[2815](https://docs.rs#2815)        out.strip_prefix("func _f():\n\t")
[2816](https://docs.rs#2816)            .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix('\n'))
[2817](https://docs.rs#2817)            .unwrap_or(&out)
[2818](https://docs.rs#2818)            .to_owned()
[2819](https://docs.rs#2819)    }

[2926](https://docs.rs#2926)    fn multiline_lambda_collapses_when_single_statement_else_kept() {
[2927](https://docs.rs#2927)        // gdformat inlines a multi-line lambda whose body is a single simple statement once the

[2935](https://docs.rs#2935)        let multi = "func _r():\n\tx.connect(func() -> void:\n\t\ta()\n\t\tb()\n\t)\n";

[2939](https://docs.rs#2939)            "func _r():\n\tx.connect(\n\t\tfunc() -> void:\n\t\t\ta()\n\t\t\tb()\n\t)\n"
[2940](https://docs.rs#2940)        );
[2941](https://docs.rs#2941)        assert!(parses_clean(&out), "{out:?}");
[2942](https://docs.rs#2942)        assert_eq!(fmt(&out), out, "idempotent");
[2943](https://docs.rs#2943)    }

[3010](https://docs.rs#3010)                super::same_significant_tokens(src, &out),

[3012](https://docs.rs#3012)            );
[3013](https://docs.rs#3013)            assert_eq!(format(&out, &cfg), out, "idempotent: {out:?}");

[3044](https://docs.rs#3044)    }

[3493](https://docs.rs#3493)    #[test]
[3494](https://docs.rs#3494)    fn redundant_grouping_parens_are_stripped() {
[3495](https://docs.rs#3495)        // gdformat strips parens that merely group a standalone expression (value / condition /
[3496](https://docs.rs#3496)        // iterable / argument / element / nested), but keeps precedence-significant ones.
[3497](https://docs.rs#3497)        assert_eq!(fmt("var x = (y)\n"), "var x = y\n");
[3498](https://docs.rs#3498)        assert_eq!(
[3499](https://docs.rs#3499)            fmt("func f():\n\treturn (g(a))\n"),
[3500](https://docs.rs#3500)            "func f():\n\treturn g(a)\n"
[3501](https://docs.rs#3501)        );
[3502](https://docs.rs#3502)        assert_eq!(
[3503](https://docs.rs#3503)            fmt("func f():\n\tfor i in (a * b):\n\t\tpass\n"),
[3504](https://docs.rs#3504)            "func f():\n\tfor i in a * b:\n\t\tpass\n"
[3505](https://docs.rs#3505)        );
[3506](https://docs.rs#3506)        assert_eq!(fmt("var a = g((x))\n"), "var a = g(x)\n"); // call arg + nested
[3507](https://docs.rs#3507)        assert_eq!(fmt("var a = {(k): (v)}\n"), "var a = {k: v}\n");
[3508](https://docs.rs#3508)        // precedence parens kept; an expr-statement assignment RHS keeps its parens (gdformat does too)
[3509](https://docs.rs#3509)        assert_eq!(fmt("var a = (b + c) * d\n"), "var a = (b + c) * d\n");
[3510](https://docs.rs#3510)        assert_eq!(fmt("func f():\n\tx = (y)\n"), "func f():\n\tx = (y)\n");
[3511](https://docs.rs#3511)    }

[3534](https://docs.rs#3534)        // `Fmt.format(…)["text"]` is a dot-chain ending in a subscript; when the flat subscriptee
[3535](https://docs.rs#3535)        // overflows, gdformat wraps leading-dot, keeping `. format(…)["text"]` (call then index) on
[3536](https://docs.rs#3536)        // one segment line. (Routes `IndexExpr`-on-a-chain through the dot-chain formatter.)
[3537](https://docs.rs#3537)        let src = "func f():\n\tvar no_space: String = Fmt.format(src, {\"singleAttributePerLine\": true, \"insertSpaceBeforeSelfClose\": false})[\"text\"]\n";
[3538](https://docs.rs#3538)        let out = fmt(src);
[3539](https://docs.rs#3539)        assert!(
[3540](https://docs.rs#3540)            out.contains("\tvar no_space: String = (\n\t\tFmt\n"),
[3541](https://docs.rs#3541)            "leading-dot: {out:?}"
[3542](https://docs.rs#3542)        );
[3543](https://docs.rs#3543)        assert!(
[3544](https://docs.rs#3544)            out.contains("\n\t\t. format(src, {") && out.contains("})[\"text\"]\n"),
[3545](https://docs.rs#3545)            "call+index segment: {out:?}"
[3546](https://docs.rs#3546)        );
[3547](https://docs.rs#3547)        assert!(parses_clean(&out), "{out:?}");
[3548](https://docs.rs#3548)        assert_eq!(fmt(&out), out, "idempotent");
[3549](https://docs.rs#3549)    }
[3550](https://docs.rs#3550)
[3551](https://docs.rs#3551)    #[test]

[3805](https://docs.rs#3805)    #[test]
[3806](https://docs.rs#3806)    fn canonical_string_rules() {
[3807](https://docs.rs#3807)        use super::canonical_string as c;
[3808](https://docs.rs#3808)        assert_eq!(c("'simple'"), "\"simple\""); // prefer double
[3809](https://docs.rs#3809)        assert_eq!(c("\"already\""), "\"already\""); // unchanged
[3810](https://docs.rs#3810)        assert_eq!(c("'has \"x\" in'"), "'has \"x\" in'"); // more " than ' -> keep single
[3811](https://docs.rs#3811)        assert_eq!(c("'a\\'b'"), "\"a'b\""); // escaped ' -> double, unescaped
[3812](https://docs.rs#3812)        assert_eq!(c("'both \" and \\' x'"), "\"both \\\" and ' x\""); // tie -> double, re-escape
[3813](https://docs.rs#3813)        assert_eq!(c("&'name'"), "&\"name\""); // StringName prefix kept
[3814](https://docs.rs#3814)        assert_eq!(c("^'a/b'"), "^\"a/b\""); // NodePath prefix kept
[3815](https://docs.rs#3815)        assert_eq!(c("r'raw\\n'"), "r\"raw\\n\""); // raw: body verbatim
[3816](https://docs.rs#3816)        assert_eq!(c("r'has \"x\"'"), "r'has \"x\"'"); // raw with " -> keep single (cannot escape)
[3817](https://docs.rs#3817)        // gdformat collapses a single-line triple-SINGLE to a regular string; triple-double + any
[3818](https://docs.rs#3818)        // multi-line triple are left verbatim.
[3819](https://docs.rs#3819)        assert_eq!(c("'''triple'''"), "\"triple\"");
[3820](https://docs.rs#3820)        assert_eq!(c("'''say \"hi\"'''"), "'say \"hi\"'"); // body has " -> regular single
[3821](https://docs.rs#3821)        assert_eq!(c("\"\"\"triple\"\"\""), "\"\"\"triple\"\"\""); // triple-double verbatim
[3822](https://docs.rs#3822)        assert_eq!(c("'''line1\nline2'''"), "'''line1\nline2'''"); // multi-line verbatim
[3823](https://docs.rs#3823)        assert_eq!(c("'\\t\\n'"), "\"\\t\\n\""); // non-quote escapes preserved
[3824](https://docs.rs#3824)    }
[3825](https://docs.rs#3825)
[3826](https://docs.rs#3826)    #[test]

[3829](https://docs.rs#3829)        assert_eq!(fmt("var b = 'has \"x\" in'\n"), "var b = 'has \"x\" in'\n");

`static func`, 1 around nested ones; comments/annotations attached to a def move with it). On

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.reflow)

`reflow: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Wrap a single-line statement that exceeds [ line_width](https://docs.rs/struct.FmtConfig.html#structfield.line_width) and contains a
bracketed group (call / array / dict / parameter list) — flat → compact → exploded, matching
gdformat’s length-driven layout. On by default. Token-preserving (no trailing comma added).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.normalize_strings)

the body has more `"` than `'`. On by default. Preserves the string’s value (a token-mutating

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.expand_inline_blocks)

`expand_inline_blocks: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Split an inline suite body onto its own indented line (`if c: x` → `if c:` / `x`,
`func f(): return` → split, `a; b` → two lines), matching gdformat. An inline *lambda* body
(`func(): x`) is preserved. On by default. Token-preserving (adds only newlines/indent).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.strip_parens)

`strip_parens: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Remove redundant grouping parens from a *standalone-expression* position — a var/const/return
value, a `for` iterable, an `if`/`while` condition, a call argument, an array/dict element, a

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.collapse_lambdas)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.safe_mode)

# format_range in gdscript_fmt - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-fmt/0.5.4/gdscript_fmt/fn.format_range.html

## Expand description

Format only the part of `source` overlapping the byte range `sel` (for editor “format selection”
/ LSP `textDocument/rangeFormatting`). The whole document is formatted for correct structure and
indentation; the result is the **minimal changed line-hunk** that intersects `sel`, or `None` if
nothing in the selection’s lines changes. Applying the edit yields the same bytes the whole-file
[`format`] would have produced for that region.

---

# format in gdscript_fmt - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gdscript-fmt/0.5.4/gdscript_fmt/fn.format.html

## Expand description

Format `source`, returning the tidied text. In `safe_mode` (the default) this returns `source`
unchanged rather than risk a meaning-changing edit (a syntax error in the input, or output whose
significant tokens differ from the input’s).

The source’s line-ending style is preserved: a file using `\r\n` (a Windows checkout) is
formatted internally in `\n` and re-emitted with `\r\n`, so the formatter never churns every line
by flipping CRLF to LF (matching gdformat, which preserves line endings).
